## 5. Evidence-source strategy (2026-05-21)

Source: `docs/research/evidence-source-strategy-2026-05-21.md`. Purpose: decide what data sources
can safely power the next Galaxy Sports Edge intelligence layer without breaking the evidence rules.

**Architecture decision:** do not add player/ref/venue/pace factors directly to confidence yet.
Add them to the Evidence Readiness Matrix first: (1) SourceSnapshot proves a provider response
existed; (2) normalization produces an EvidenceRecord / GameSignal; (3) the Evidence Readiness
Matrix decides whether each factor is ACTIVE, SHADOW_READY, SHADOW_COLLECTING, BLOCKED, or ABSENT;
(4) scoring reads only ACTIVE factors explicitly allowed to contribute; (5) true EV remains
blocked until independent fair probability is source-backed and separately promoted.

**Provider surfaces reviewed:** The Odds API (live odds endpoint, core markets, paid quota,
historical odds/player-prop/business-tier notes, explicit API-key/header behavior —
https://theoddsapi.com/); Sportradar Sports Data API (broad official/commercial coverage —
https://docs.sportradar.com/sports-data-api); SportsDataIO (sports data, injuries, lineups/depth
charts, standings, betting data, historical odds, ID mapping, widgets, league-specific APIs —
https://sportsdata.io/); Open-Meteo (forecast and archived forecast APIs with coordinates,
hourly variables, multiple weather models, historical forecast runs —
https://open-meteo.com/en/docs).

**Provider fit:**
- **Market odds** — start here; paid key already present; deploy-readiness confirmed 20,000
  requests remaining. Use: live odds; scores/settlement; historical odds only if the current
  plan includes it. Risks: quota exhaustion inside 2 weeks; stale line movement if
  opening/current prices are not preserved; false "edge" if market-derived fair price gets
  mistaken for independent probability.
- **Player availability** — use only official/licensed injury, lineup, depth-chart feeds
  (SportsDataIO or Sportradar). Risks: late scratches; inconsistent team phrasing
  ("questionable" vs "game-time decision"); player ID mapping drift across providers. Matrix
  posture: SHADOW_ONLY until enough settled outcome history proves incremental calibration value.
- **Officials / referees** — use only licensed assignment and historical same-sport trend feeds
  (Sportradar if coverage includes official assignment; league official sources if terms permit).
  Risks: small samples; playoff/prime-time assignment bias; crew composition changes. Matrix
  posture: SHADOW_ONLY with high min sample size.
- **Venue environment** — venue coordinates + game-time weather/roof/surface state (Open-Meteo
  for weather where outdoor conditions matter; licensed schedule/venue metadata for
  roof/surface/park state). Risks: roof decisions; wind shifts near first pitch/kickoff;
  incorrectly geocoded stadiums. Matrix posture: weather can be useful quickly, but it must age
  out aggressively.
- **Pace / team rates** — use league/team stat feeds, not LLM summaries (SportsDataIO,
  Sportradar, or league APIs where legally allowed). Risks: early-season samples; injuries
  changing tempo; garbage-time distortion. Matrix posture: SHADOW_ONLY until bucket-level Brier
  improvement is measured.

**What changed in code:** `packages/prediction-engine/src/evidence-readiness-matrix.ts` plus
tests — executable definitions for market board, line movement, rest state, schedule density,
pace profile, division context, player availability, officials, venue environment, venue
history, milestone context, independent fair probability, true EV. Each factor carries: source
categories, minimum trust, minimum sample size, freshness window, scoring eligibility,
activation requirement, failure horizon, likely failure mode. "This is intentionally boring
infrastructure. It is the layer that lets the product become aggressive later without becoming
sloppy now."

---

## 6. Brand and commentary voice rules a coding agent generating copy must follow

### 6a. Galaxy Sports Edge NFL commentary brand research (2026-09-10)

Source: `docs/research/2026-09-10-galaxy-commentary-brand/final-report.md`. Every finding carries
an exact source URL; paper policy separated from observed practice; unconfirmable items marked
UNVERIFIED. Not legal advice. The account's stated posture: transformative, commentary-led,
seconds-long telestrated edits — never standalone rips or compilations.

**TOPIC 1 — how 3–5 top NFL film-breakdown creators actually operate:**
- **NFL Access Pass (2023):** opened to a "select group" of creators, granting "officially
  approved footage" with monetization allowed on YouTube; NFL executive Ian Trombetta noted
  "tight parameters" on what footage is approved (digiday.com;
  sportsbusinessjournal.com 2023-09-14). As of 2025-01-30, the Access Pass roster included
  **Brett Kollmann**, with **J.T. O'Sullivan** and **Kurt Benkert** named for Access Pass for
  Legends; Year 1 covered 24 creators and 200M+ views (sportsvideo.org 2025-01-30). Legends
  lets former players use official highlights, Super Bowl, NFL Draft, other footage while
  retaining a share of ad revenue (news.bloomberglaw.com). **Key conclusion:** Kollmann's,
  O'Sullivan's, and Benkert's current footage is at least partly **expressly licensed** — their
  survival is not proof an unaffiliated account faces the same enforcement. Copy their
  editorial structure (segmenting, telestration, slow-mo loops), not their apparent footage
  tolerance. Track and apply for Access Pass when eligible.
- **Tim Jenkins / All Things QB (Front Office Sports, 2026):** long-form 30+ min videos;
  creators "loop through the same play at different angles and use a telestrator"; Jenkins
  posts **two public videos weekly and two members-only clips**; a 30-minute episode takes
  ~**2–3 hours**, mostly identifying plays; toolchain **Hudl for telestration**, **OBS Studio**
  to record his screen, light editing after; the report expressly notes creators outside
  Access Pass are "taking a risk". Exploit: standardize repeatable screen-record → telestrate →
  loop-angles workflow (free: OBS + any telestration tool; Hudl is the paid reference). Keep a
  footage-light public version; paywalling does not cure copyright risk. UNVERIFIED: whether
  Jenkins is licensed, his exact footage source, per-play seconds, claims history.
- **All-22 sourcing:** historically Game Pass offered broadcasts and All-22; analysts described
  accessing international Game Pass, QuickTime screen-recording All-22, sharing files privately
  (Defector) — observed practice, not permission. Exploit: use legitimate viewing access
  (e.g., NFL+ NFL Pro's All-22 offering) to *study* plays, then rebuild the teaching point as
  original diagrams whenever footage rights are uncertain.
- **Enforcement history:** in 2007 the NFL objected to **20 seconds of game footage** in law
  professor Wendy Seltzer's copyright-warning video; NFL counsel: "We do not see how the use
  of such game content has any educational purposes or character" (sportsbusinessjournal.com;
  deadspin.com). A legal article reports the NFL requested removal of **more than 3,000
  YouTube clips in 2006** (gould.usc.edu). Exploit: **no safe "under X seconds" rule exists** —
  make every second necessary to active criticism (pause, annotate, narrate); avoid
  uninterrupted highlight value.
- **Closest thing to a charter:** CMSI Code of Best Practices in Fair Use for Online Video,
  Principle TWO — "Using copyrighted material for illustration or example": fair when important
  to the larger purpose but subordinate to it; fair when not presented for its original purpose
  but harnessed for a new one; illustrative quotations "should be drawn from a range of
  different sources" where possible and "no longer than is necessary to achieve the intended
  effect"; proper attribution reduces complaint likelihood (cmsimpact.org). Exploit: this is
  the argumentative frame for telestrated breakdowns — footage subordinate to analysis, used
  for teaching, kept to minimum, attributed.
- **Reconstruction/animation alternatives:** Kurt Benkert produces Madden-based teaching content
  (Front Office Sports); Samuel Gold published film-room articles with named concepts and
  original play diagrams (fieldgulls.com 2016). Exploit: when footage rights are uncertain,
  rebuild teaching points with Madden captures or original overhead dot/route diagrams.
  UNVERIFIED: whether any named creator uses animated dots/diagrams as a *systematic* footage
  substitute — build that ourselves.

**TOPIC 2 — beat reporters/outlets: reuse permissions; facts, quotations, X reposts:**
- **Facts and game results are not protected expression.** *NBA v. Motorola*, 105 F.3d 841
  (2d Cir. 1997): "Motorola and STATS did not infringe NBA's copyright because they reproduced
  only facts from the broadcasts, not the expression or description of the game that
  constitutes the broadcast"; "No author may copyright facts or ideas." Exploit: independently
  write posts from scores, down/distance, formations, play outcomes, statistics. Do not copy a
  reporter's phrasing, graphic design, database, or footage just because the underlying facts
  are free.
- **PFF — unusually explicit creator permission (updated 2026-09-04):** pff.com/terms §1.9
  permits sharing, quoting, or screenshotting **individual PFF grades, statistics, or excerpts
  of free articles** on personal, noncommercial social accounts with attribution/linking and
  without bulk substitution. §1.10 expressly permits monetized creator content (videos,
  streams, podcasts, newsletters, articles, social content) to "reference, quote, or display
  individual items of Free Content," provided each item credits PFF, links where possible, is
  not bulk/database-like, does not substitute for PFF, and is not presented as endorsed by
  PFF. Paid content, API data, and AI output excluded. Exploit: one public PFF grade/stat per
  post, labeled "Source: PFF," with a link and original analysis on top. Never publish paid-only
  tables or bulk rankings.
- **The Athletic (NYT) — no sharing clause, no CC license:** terms grant only "a limited,
  revocable, non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to access and use the Services";
  sharing only "with our prior written permission... or as expressly permitted by these
  Terms." The NYT fair-use policy is in fact a contact page for *requesting licenses* —
  operative posture is request-permission-first. Exploit: link to Athletic articles; restate
  facts independently; use short quotation only under a separate fair-use analysis. Never rely
  on "credit" as permission.
- **ESPN/Disney — restrictive terms:** personal, noncommercial consumer license only; "no
  right to reproduce, distribute, communicate to the public, make available to the public, or
  transform any Disney Product"; no "use the Disney Products for any commercial or
  business-related use or build a business utilizing the Disney Products," except where
  applicable law overrides (disneytermsofuse.com). Exploit: link out; use platform-native
  sanctioned sharing; extract independently restated facts and short quotations under
  fair-use analysis only.
- **X reposts and quote posts:** X's 2026 terms — users retain ownership but grant X a
  worldwide license authorizing X to make content available and "let others do the same,"
  including "syndication, broadcast, distribution, repost, promotion or publication," subject
  to X's terms — this licenses **X and its sublicensees**, not a user downloading and
  re-uploading someone else's video. Quote post mechanics (2026 guide): click repost icon →
  select Quote → "Write your take above the embedded original" → post; "Quote posting wraps
  the original in your own commentary... The commentary sits above the embedded post, so your
  text gets read first." Exploit: quote-post official @NFL and team posts — the original
  stays embedded and attributed, commentary lives in *our* post. Never download and re-upload
  their video files. UNVERIFIED: no current official X help-center article documenting
  repost/quote was locatable; the ToS-based reading is the strongest available basis.
- **Quotations — no bright-line rule:** the U.S. Copyright Office: "there is no formula to
  ensure that a predetermined percentage or amount of a work — or specific number of words,
  lines, pages, copies — may be used without permission." Even a small amount can weigh
  against fair use if it is the "heart" of the work (*Harper & Row v. Nation*). Exploit:
  quote only what is needed to identify and critique the source; surrounding original
  analysis should dominate. Never promise "1–2 sentences" is automatically fair.
- **NFL press releases vs. NFL footage — separate the two:** NFL.com/news press-release content
  (signings, rule changes, statements) is routinely and freely quotable/redistributable as news
  with attribution. That practice concerns **text**, not game footage; nothing in it waives
  rights over broadcast/game video. Exploit: quote press releases and official statements
  freely with attribution; treat footage under an entirely separate analysis.

**TOPIC 3 — underused zero-cost opportunities:**
- **YouTube embeds** expressly licensed through the Service: "You may also show YouTube videos
  through the embeddable YouTube player"; uploaders grant use "only as enabled by a feature of
  the Service (such as video playback or embeds)" — does not authorize use independent of
  YouTube. Exploit: embed official NFL YouTube videos on a website (player intact); does NOT
  authorize cropping footage into an independently uploaded X video.
- **Getty Embed** — real zero-dollar option with hard limits: 70M+ photos on a **noncommercial**
  website or blog — not for selling, raising money, promotion, or endorsement; editorial/
  newsworthy/public-interest purposes only; no advertising, promotions, merchandising, implied
  endorsement, unlawful use, or display outside the Embedded Viewer; Getty may remove content or
  monetize the viewer. Exploit: use Getty's own embed player in a non-promotional editorial
  site article. Do not download Getty images or place them in X graphics, thumbnails, ads, or
  sales pages.
- **GIPHY embed vs. reuse:** support page instructs select "Embed," choose iframe or HTML5,
  paste code, publish; GIPHY terms: "we grant each user of the Services a worldwide,
  non-exclusive, non-sublicensable and non-transferable license to use Content solely for
  purposes of using the Services. Use, reproduction, modification, distribution or storage of
  any Content for other than purposes of using the Services is expressly prohibited without
  prior written permission." Historical context: a 2016 NFL–GIPHY "test agreement" made Giphy
  "the source of high quality and authentic NFL GIFs of ancillary game and historical/iconic
  content" — **not gameplay GIFs** (techcrunch.com 2016-12-02). Exploit: use GIPHY's hosted
  embed/player where an official NFL GIF exists; never download and re-upload GIFs to X.
  UNVERIFIED: whether an official @NFL GIPHY channel is currently active with current uploads.
- **Wikimedia Commons** — genuinely free NFL game photos (not video): Commons hosts NFL game
  photos (e.g., All-Pro Reels transfers from Flickr via #flickr2commons, 2021 Washington at
  Falcons). Exploit: use as thumbnails, post headers, site imagery with required attribution.
  **Caution (UNVERIFIED per file):** confirm each file's license field before commercial/
  monetized use.
- **AP Images** — priced, not free; public a la carte accounts exist. A 2014 report: editorial
  web use for two years of one photo ~$95 (poynter.org). Price UNVERIFIED as current. USA Today
  Sports Images similarly licensed stock; no zero-dollar editorial embed tier located.
- **No current official fan clip-sharing tool found** (UNVERIFIED — feature not located): no
  current NFL app / NFL+ "make your own clip and share to social" feature in public
  documentation. What exists: NFL+ "NFL Pro" offers **All-22 Coaches Film for every game
  dating back to the 2022 season**, playlist saving/sharing — viewing/playlist features, not
  re-upload rights (sportsvideo.org 2024-08-21). The 2008-era NFL.com "Replay Re-Cutter" is
  discontinued. Notably even **teams** historically could not create their own gameplay GIFs and
  had to rely on the NFL's social team (large violation fines) — the league does not take a
  permissive posture on third-party gameplay-video redistribution.
- **The pre-1964 public-domain avenue exists but is item-specific:** Library of Congress —
  "Published works registered for copyright in the U.S. through Dec. 31, 1963 are now in the
  public domain **unless the copyright was renewed**" — and the only way to determine renewal
  status is a copyright search. Exploit: genuine path for historical material, but requires a
  **per-item renewal search** — archive.org hosting alone proves nothing. Default assumption
  for any NFL footage: still under copyright unless an item-specific search says otherwise.
- **Public-domain NFL footage is not established (general rule):** Internet Archive hosts
  batches labeled 1945/1956/1959 NFL seasons, but the preservation project itself says some
  material cannot be uploaded due to copyright constraints; the NFL has affirmatively claimed
  copyright over historic footage such as Super Bowl I. Exploit: do not use "old NFL footage"
  merely because it is old or archived; use only items with an item-specific rights statement,
  renewal search, or written permission; build original diagrams from historical facts instead.

**Appendix items deliberately excluded:** a PDF at an assets.website-files.com URL titled "The
Athletic Cos. Website Terms of Use" was not confirmed to be the NYT-owned Athletic (the real
NYT terms were used instead); forum/Reddit speculation about creator copyright treatment was
treated as non-evidence; disclaimers ("all rights go to...," "no infringement intended") grant
no permission — noted, not used.

### 6b. Pundit-signal legal research framework (2026-06-13)

Source: `docs/research/pundit-signal-legal-research-prompt.md`. A deep-research prompt engineered
for a reasoning model, designed to map every LAWFUL path to "use the analytical substance of
sports-pundit commentary as a graded input signal in a commercial prediction product, without
infringing copyright or breaching contract" — and to stress-test every avenue against actual
case law, not rationalize a predetermined answer. Context: SiriusXM Fantasy Sports Radio shows
(e.g. "Elite Sports with Jeff Mans"); constraints already known: SiriusXM's Customer Agreement
(§9 / "AI Matters") restricts content to personal, non-commercial use, prohibits using their
content to create, train, or improve any AI service, prohibits scraping/recording/automated
extraction; content is account-gated (paid subscription) and copyrighted broadcast expression.
Many pundits also publish public podcasts (e.g. "One MANS Opinion" on Podbean/Apple) under
different terms.

**Research questions the framework requires answered with citations:** (A) copyright line —
facts vs expression (Feist v. Rural Telephone 1991; 17 U.S.C. §102(b)); is a pundit's
prediction/opinion protectable or unprotectable once expressed; human-authored original
summaries/paraphrases vs machine paraphrase of a fixed transcript (derivative work).
(B) Fair use — all four factors of 17 U.S.C. §107 applied to (a) human-authored attributed
paraphrase log used commercially, (b) storing verbatim transcript for internal AI training;
**the key adverse case: Fox News Network v. TVEyes (2d Cir. 2018)** — search/transcription vs
clipping holdings; **the key AI-training cases: Thomson Reuters v. Ross Intelligence
(D. Del. 2025 — fair use REJECTED for AI training on Westlaw headnotes)** and pending
NYT v. OpenAI, Authors Guild v. OpenAI; contrast with the fair-use winners **Authors Guild v.
Google (2d Cir. 2015)** and **A.V. ex rel. Vanderhye v. iParadigms (Turnitin)** — which side of
the line does "ingest pundit transcripts to improve a commercial prediction model" fall on?
(C) Contract & access — ToS enforceability independent of copyright (can contract bar a use
copyright would permit?); CFAA post-**Van Buren v. United States (2021)** and **hiQ v.
LinkedIn**; is there any "data laundering" doctrine (hypothesis to test: the breach attaches
at the moment of prohibited *use*, regardless of output form). (D) Hot-news misappropriation
(INS v. AP; NBA v. Motorola, 2d Cir. 1997) — could time-sensitive pundit picks be protected,
and does it change near-real-time ingestion? (E) The licensing path (most likely real "yes") —
who owns SiriusXM original programming rights (network, production company, host); media-
monitoring license structures/pricing for small companies; licensed intermediaries/vendors
already relicensing sports-media commentary; content-partnership/affiliate structures with
pundits directly. (F) The public-feed path — podcast platform terms (Podbean/Apple/YouTube)
for automated transcription and derived analytics for commercial use; Creative-Commons or
openly-licensed sports-commentary sources. (G) Precedent in the wild — how consensus-pick
aggregators and tout-grading sites source data lawfully (license, public data, user-submitted,
first-party); open-source rights-respecting ingestion patterns (provenance tracking, license
gating, transcript-rights metadata).

**Required output format:** executive verdict (2–3 viable lawful paths ranked by viability ×
cost × effort; dead paths with one-line reason + controlling authority); path-by-path analysis
(legal basis with citations, concrete steps, cost/effort, residual risk, what to confirm with
retained counsel); the "no" list (each dead path, the controlling case/clause, why a technical
workaround does or does not change the outcome); citations appendix (every case, statute, ToS
clause, vendor, source with a working link and one-line relevance note); counsel brief (1-page
summary the founder can hand to an IP attorney).

**Rules for the research model:** cite or don't claim — every legal proposition gets primary-
source support; distinguish copyright from contract from CFAA at every step — they fail
independently; be current (2023–2026 AI-training fair-use law); if a path requires a license,
say so plainly rather than implying a free workaround exists; flag uncertainty honestly; mark
anything unsettled. This is not legal advice; every claim carries a citation or nothing.

## 7. Metrics, methods, and theories not covered elsewhere

### 7a. The intelligence-pass review framework (2026-09-12)

Source: `docs/research/intelligence-pass-prompt.md`. A prompt for a reasoning agent to audit
Galaxy Sports Edge — explicitly NOT a code review but an adversarial think-through: find what's
missing, what's wrong, what could be dramatically better. Read `AGENTS.md` first (carries full
system context, laws, session history). The six audit areas, in priority order:

1. **Calibration mathematics** — the product's credibility. Floors: n>=100, Brier<=0.22,
   ECE<=0.05 (debiased). Selective path: delta=0.1, rank on marketFairProb. Skill metrics:
   Brier Skill Score, Negative Log Likelihood, Murphy decomposition (REL/RES/UNC), null-band
   ECE. Pushes excluded from win rates. Published line snaps to nearest book quote (not
   consensus mean). Key questions: is the debiased ECE estimator correct — does the plug-in
   noise subtraction `max(0, raw - noise)` over-subtract when a real gap exists? Is the
   selective gate (delta=0.1 on marketFairProb) the right structure — what would a Bayesian
   approach look like? Should CRPS or log score join the public surface? The market's own
   price (marketFairProb) is the best-calibrated forecaster (**Brier 0.197 vs 0.231 for
   confidence on 469 rows**) — what does this tell us about the model architecture? **CLV
   beat-close is 23% vs 52.4% required** — this is the ESTABLISHED blocker; what's the root
   cause — line timing, market efficiency, or selection bias?
2. **DFS optimizer correctness** — exact dynamic programming over (roster-slot fill state) ×
   (salary bucket); provably optimal for the given objective. Questions: is the leverage
   formula `leverage = ceiling / (proj * own)` correct — does it properly capture contrarian
   upside? Is one-solver-per-stacked-team the right QB stacking formulation? Cash mode
   maximizes projection (median); GPP maximizes ceiling — is ceiling the right GPP objective,
   or should it be top-percentile of simulated outcomes? Exposure control: maxExp is a
   1–100% per-player cap across generated lineups — is greedy rejection optimal, or should
   exposure be integrated into the DP? What's missing vs LineStar — Consensus, Cons Diff,
   AlertScore, SIC Score, Safety, Imp Pts, vs Pos rank, Range (floor-to-ceiling spread) — and
   which would actually improve lineup quality?
3. **Player ranking system (GSE Score)** — 0–100; LIVE reads processGrade from nflverse;
   SAMPLE is pool percentile. Questions: is pool percentile the right SAMPLE ranking — z-score
   or percentile-of-position? The expected-metrics module fits its own CPOE/RYOE/xYAC models
   on nflverse play-by-play and proves them against NGS — is linear regression on play
   features adequate, or should it be gradient-boosted? Value currently `value = proj /
   salary * 1000` — is points-per-$1k the right value metric?
4. **Visual design and motion** — the Field visual system: near-black ground (#08090C), bone
   text (#EDE8E0), one ember signal (#FF4D2E). Five nav destinations trimmed to four
   (Board / Players / Fantasy / GSN). Questions: ticker at 90s per loop — readable? Does the
   homepage canvas hero compete with content or enhance it? Does the board page's cinematic
   opening earn its keep or is it decoration? Door-card hover rail animation timing right?
   What ONE visual change would most improve perceived quality?
5. **Copy and communication** — every customer-facing string must pass: "would a sharp friend
   who actually plays DFS say this?" Questions: remaining jargon a normal person wouldn't
   understand? Are empty states honest AND clear? Does the homepage communicate what the
   product IS in under 5 seconds?
6. **Data flow and factor engine** — founder-picks factor engine composes: depth chart,
   injury, matchup split, underlying metrics, consensus, rest. Questions: the factor engine
   treats missing data as ABSENT (never zero) — is this the right default? The Statcast loader
   fetches season-aggregate CSVs — should it cache, and what's the refresh cadence? What
   factors are NOT computed that would materially improve pick quality (weather, travel,
   referee tendencies, public money splits)?

**Explicitly NOT to do:** do not rewrite code — describe what should change and why; do not
audit every file — focus on the six areas; do not check every test — trust the guardrails
unless something looks wrong; do not re-derive what AGENTS.md already documents.

**Output format:** per area — one insight probably missing (the non-obvious thing), one
concrete recommendation with implementation detail, one risk of changing it. End with a
priority ranking of recommendations. Be direct: say what's wrong; say what's already
excellent — knowing what NOT to change is as valuable as knowing what to fix.

### 7b. The gse-lab computation program (2026-09-17)

Source: `docs/research/2026-09-17/gse-lab/COMPUTATION_NOTES.md` + README pointer. "Worker B"
computed 29 CSVs, 15 metric families, 4 scripts from nflverse play-by-play — "every number
computed by script from downloaded nflverse play-by-play. No mock data, no copied tables."
Raw downloads: `play_by_play_{2025,2026}.csv.gz` + `ftn_charting_2025.csv` from the
nflverse-data GitHub releases; excluded as reproducible downloads (not vendored), along with
Python venvs. Provenance: nflverse CC-BY 4.0 (credit "nflverse"); FTN charting CC-BY-SA 4.0
(credit "FTN Data via nflverse", share-alike). 2025: 48,771 raw plays, 285 games (weeks
1–18 REG + 19–22 POST); analysis uses REG only (46,452 REG → 29,239 after filters). 2026:
Week 1 only — 16 games, 2,756 raw → 1,673 filtered.

**The shared filters (exact, every team file uses them):**
1. `season_type == 'REG'` (2025 file contains postseason weeks 19–22).
2. `play_type in ('pass','run')` — no punts/FGs/kickoffs in the efficiency sample.
3. `qb_kneel == 0`, `qb_spike == 0` (453 kneels + 82 spikes in 2025 excluded).
4. **Garbage time:** exclude plays with `qtr == 4 AND (wp > 0.95 OR wp < 0.05)` on the nflfastR
   possession-team win probability — removed 3,702 plays in 2025 (11.2%), 238 in 2026 week 1
   (12.4%). OT (qtr == 5) is NOT filtered — every OT play is high leverage by construction.
5. **Success = EPA > 0** (nflfastR convention; verified `(success == 1) == (epa > 0)` on 100% of
   pass/run plays, 0 mismatches).
6. **Dropback** = `pass_attempt == 1` OR `qb_scramble == 1` (4for4 convention; verified
   `sack==1` implies `pass_attempt==1`; scrambles count as dropbacks). 2025: 17,626 dropbacks;
   2026 wk1: 1,015.
7. **Designed rush** = `rush_attempt == 1` AND `qb_scramble == 0` AND `qb_kneel == 0`.
8. **Explosive play** = 15+ yards on a dropback or 10+ yards on a designed rush (4for4
   convention; other providers use 20-yard passes — do not compare across conventions).
9. EPA/EPA model: the `epa`/`ep` columns ship in nflverse and come from the **nflfastR
   Expected Points model** (multinomial logistic regression on down/distance/field position);
   not re-estimated — EPA taken as published.

**Metric families (the 15):** team EPA/play + success rate (offense and sign-flipped defense),
EPA distributions (n, mean, p10/p25/median/p75/p90, share_neg_epa, share_chunk_epa with
EPA > 1.0), weekly trends (544 rows: 32 teams × 17 weeks), unit matchups (pass_off/rush_off
EPA + success, pass_def/rush_def sign-flipped, stuff rates, percentile ranks), drive stats
(deliberately on the *unfiltered* REG sample — punts/FGs/garbage-time drives are real drives;
td_rate, fg_rate, punt_rate, three_and_out_rate = exactly 3 plays ending in Punt,
turnover_drive_rate including pick-sixes, downs_rate, avg_drive_start_own; league 2025:
2.10 points/drive, 24.0% TD rate, 20.4% three-and-out, 11.1% turnover-drive rate, avg start
own 30.4 — all at known NFL norms), down splits (early_1_2 vs late_3_4), extra metrics
(stuff rate, stuff allowed, air_epa/yac_epa/air_yards per dropback and allowed versions,
late-and-close EPA = 4th quarter with possession-team wp in [0.20, 0.80], ~50–80
plays/team/season, always reported with n), league percentiles (pct = (rank−1)/(n−1)×100,
100 = best, lower-is-better metrics inverted), kicker metrics (FG attempts and make rate by
distance bucket <30/30–39/40–49/50+, XP make rate, kicking points/game, FG/XP EPA per
attempt, kicker names from `kicker_player_name`; 2025 league: FG 85.6%, XP 95.9%, 7.36
kicking pts/game), defense detail (INT forced rate/dropback, forced fumble rate/play,
opponent fumble recovery share, TFL rate/rush, takeaway rate/drive, defensive TD rate/drive,
points allowed/drive), special teams (kickoff touchback rate, opponent avg start after
kickoffs, kickoff/punt EPA, kick/punt return EPA and yards/return, FG/punt/XP blocks forced;
2025 league: 20.5% touchback rate, opp avg start own 29.8, kickoff EPA −0.257/kick —
kicking off is negative-EPA in the dynamic-kickoff era, punt EPA −0.127/punt, 23 FG blocks /
9 punt blocks / 12 XP blocks), turnover luck decomposition, player first-downs, QB
aggressiveness, 4-man-rush vs pressure.

**Turnover luck (actual vs expected):** expected INTs = league-average INT rate per dropback
× team dropbacks (2025 baseline **1.867%**, 2026 wk1 2.069%); expected fumbles lost =
league-average fumble-lost rate per play × team plays (2025 **0.640%**, 2026 wk1 1.076%);
`*_diff_actual_minus_expected`: negative = lucky, positive = unlucky. Same construction on
defense for takeaways. Occurrence-vs-recovery luck layer: occurrence (partially skill) =
forced fumbles per play vs league-rate expectation; recovery (near-pure noise) = recovery
share minus league mean (2025: **46.3%**) — fumble recovery year-to-year correlation ~0.00
(pure noise), forced-fumble occurrence weak repeatability. Textbook 2025 case: DET forced 19
fumbles (+6.5 over expected) but recovered only 26.3% (−20 pts vs league) — process good,
results unlucky, positive regression expected. The Dallas 2025 demo: DAL finished 7-9-1
(StatMuse) despite +0.135 EPA/play (4th) and 27.7 ppg — offense threw 5.2 fewer INTs than
expected, but the defense generated 4.6 fewer INTs than expected and the team lost 1.7 more
fumbles than expected — textbook efficiency-vs-record split. **Turnover-worthy-play proxy
(2025 only):** FTN `is_interception_worthy` charting joined at 100% coverage on
(game_id, play_id); ~3.0% of dropbacks flagged; 52.3% of flagged throws were actual INTs;
reported as `int_worthy_throw_rate` per dropback. Not available for 2026 (no FTN 2026
charting at first; later: `ftn_charting_2026.csv` downloaded 2026-09-17, Week 1 only,
458,719 bytes, joins 2026 pbp at 100% on dropbacks — the @GridironInfo_ FTN-charting+nflverse
chart for 2026 Week 1 is reproducible from this stack).

**Pressure — NOT AVAILABLE, partial proxies provided:** the nflverse FTN charting subset has
**no hurry/pressure columns** — true pressure rate (hurries + hits + sacks) **cannot be
computed** from this data. Proxies with explicit caveat: `qb_hit_rate_allowed/forced`
(nflverse `qb_hit` flag; ~6% of sacks coded without a qb_hit) and `sack_rate_allowed/forced`
per dropback — these UNDERESTIMATE true pressure. Real pressure needs PFF/SIS/ESPN charting
(paid or manually scraped), per the catalog. **Literature application:** pressure generation
is sticky, but pressure-to-sack conversion is near-pure luck (R² < 0.005) — hence the props
desk deliberately projects no individual sack props.

**Derived-but-exact constructions:** TFL rate — no `tackle_for_loss` column exists in nflverse
pbp; computed as opponent designed rushes with `yards_gained < 0` ÷ opponent designed rushes
(exact by definition, but computed, not charted — will not match charting vendors' counts
exactly). Drive identification: a drive = one `(game_id, fixed_drive)` group; offensive team =
majority `posteam` over scrimmage plays; result = last play's `fixed_drive_result`; points =
offense's score differential across the drive (captures PATs, 2-pt conversions, safeties
exactly). **Kickoff bookkeeping (verified empirically):** on a kickoff play, `posteam` = the
RETURN team and `defteam` = the KICKING team, and the kickoff groups into the return team's
drive; touchback spot in 2025 = the **35**-yard line (post-2024 dynamic-kickoff rule);
`opp_avg_start_after_kickoff` excludes 93/2785 kickoffs where the kicking team kept possession
(onside kicks cannot be identified — no column). **EPA bundling caveat:** nflverse has NO
per-return EPA column; play-level `epa` on a kickoff/punt bundles kick/punt WITH its return —
return EPA figures are return-inclusive play EPA, not isolated return skill.

**Player first-downs / QB aggressiveness:** same filtered sample; rushing first-down rate
per player (includes QB scrambles — lands on the QB's row, documented); receiving first-down
rate per reception and per target; qualifiers 2025: 50+ rushes OR 30+ targets (225 players),
2026 Week 1: 8+/8+ (55 players, role check). 2025 extremes: rush FD% leaders T.Lawrence
(52.1%, 71 rushes), J.Allen (49.4%) — QB scrambles inflate QB rows; receiving leaders
T.McLaurin (88.9%), A.Pierce (87.8%) on 30+ receptions. Team = modal `posteam`. 2026 data
confirmed structural breaks: **D.Montgomery → HOU** (20 rushes wk1), **D.Moore → BUF**
(8 targets, 5 receptions wk1) — from the data, not memory. QB aggressiveness: aDOT =
Σ`air_yards` ÷ attempts with non-null air_yards (sacks excluded by construction); CPOE from
nflfastR `cp` in percentage points (nflverse ships `cpoe` on 0–100 scale; verified
`cpoe == 100*(complete_pass - cp)` on 100% of non-null rows); 2025 aDOT leaders M.Mariota
10.18, D.Maye 9.36, M.Stafford 9.30; CPOE leaders D.Maye +10.6, B.Purdy +7.6, J.Love +6.2;
worst B.Cook −12.6, D.Gabriel −8.5, S.Sanders −7.0 (Maye's +10.6 consistent with MVP-caliber
2025: NE 14–3, +0.186 EPA/play). `adot_pct`: higher = deeper (style descriptor, NOT better).
No SIS on-target rate — proprietary, not replicable; CPOE from the nflfastR `cp` model is
the honest public proxy. **4-man rush rate:** share of dropbacks with `n_pass_rushers == 4`
(FTN charting); rows with 0 excluded as a data quirk (54 in 2025, 4 in 2026 wk1); sanity
check vs @GridironInfo_ 2026 Wk1 reference (chart BUF ~65%/19% pressure, DET ~60%/12%):
computed BUF 64.3%/21.4%, DET 63.5%/14.3% — 4-man rates match within a point, pressure proxy
runs 2–3 pts higher, ordinal agreement holds (BUF > DET on both). 2025: BUF 70.4%/16.0%,
DET 64.3%/14.4%.

**Known limitations (stated in the notes):** nothing is opponent-adjusted — DVOA-style
adjustment is the known next step; 2026 files are one-game samples (~45–65 filtered plays per
team; JAX +0.400 dominated by one blowout) — do NOT treat as ratings; the catalog's
DAVE/shrinkage lesson applies double; `qb_hit` undercounts pressure; 2026 `int_worthy_*`
initially NaN; drive counts exclude garbage-time/kneel drives so points_per_drive is
approximate; single league INT/fumble baseline — a downfield-throw-rate-adjusted baseline
would be better (not attempted); weekly_trends excludes garbage-time plays so blowout weeks
read slightly different from unfiltered sources; `share_chunk_epa` (EPA > 1.0) and 10th/90th
percentiles noisy for 2026 single-game samples; no passes-defensed column (omitted, not
proxied); no isolated return-only EPA; no onside-kick identification.

**Sanity checks run (independent sources, nothing copied):** 2025 standings/EPA agreement
(NE +0.186 EPA/play top-5: NE, LA, GB, DAL, BUF; StatMuse standings NE 14-3, BUF 12-5, LA
12-5 consistent; PFF final 2025 power rankings LAR #1, SEA #2, BUF #3 with Buffalo "third
in EPA per play" vs my 5th +0.132 — within filter noise; independent GitHub EPA analysis
rstrube92: GB pass EPA +0.278 vs mine +0.288, NE run EPA −0.074 vs mine −0.050 — same story;
SEA defense leader +0.112; Seahawks won Super Bowl LX 29-13 over NE; magnitudes match
published EPA scales — elite ≈ +0.13–0.19/play, worst ≈ −0.17–−0.23/play). 2026 Week 1 vs
FTN DVOA: FTN "Jacksonville would be first unadjusted after their 34-10 win over Cleveland"
— mine JAX #1 (+0.400); FTN named CHI top offense (mine CHI #3 +0.360, 59 pts); PIT top
defense (mine PIT def-EPA #2 +0.321 behind JAX +0.493); FTN ranks SF #1 overall *after*
opponent adjustment (SF beat the SB-favorite Rams 27-7 in Australia) — mine SF #5 (+0.262)
unadjusted; all differences explained by their opponent adjustment which I do not apply.
Scores in the data match public reporting exactly (JAX 34–CLE 10, BUF 36–HOU 31, NE 10–SEA
13, CHI 59–CAR 37). Seattle defense 2025: The Athletic (TruMedia) reported SEA led league in
defensive EPA 12.5/100 snaps (+0.125/play) vs mine +0.112/play — same rank, magnitude
within ~11% (filter differences). Buffalo offense 2025: PFF said BUF 3rd in EPA/play and
2nd in success rate vs mine 5th (+0.132) and 5th (0.4864) — same neighborhood, attributable
to my 11% garbage-time exclusion. BUF 2025 EPA/play percentile 87.1 (5th), DET 74.2 (9th).
**The Buffalo-vs-Detroit Week 2 sheet (2025 baselines):** BUF pass off +0.174 (84th pct)
vs DET pass def +0.014 (61st); BUF rush off +0.078 vs DET rush def −0.001; DET pass off
+0.168 (81st) vs BUF pass def +0.108 (94th); DET rush off −0.055 vs BUF rush def −0.064.
Both attacks pass-first by EPA; both run defenses below average.

### 7c. The props-consensus projection pipeline (2026-09-17)

Source: `docs/research/2026-09-17/props-consensus/our-metric-stack.md` (+ `game-projections.md`
worked example for Bills–Lions TNF). "Computed data only — no mock data, no copied tables."

**How a number becomes a projection:**
1. **Base prior = 2025 full-season per-game means** computed from the filtered sample (never
   quoted from anywhere).
2. **Week 1 2026 is a role-check only:** confirms roster continuity and target/carry shares
   (and caught real structural breaks — Montgomery to Houston, DJ Moore to Buffalo) but
   contributes **zero weight to any efficiency rate** (100% 2025 / 0% Week 1 for efficiency).
3. Volume is **script-adjusted** — measured 2025 dropback rates by win-probability bucket move
   a favorite toward running and an underdog toward passing.
4. Then **garbage-time corrected** — because props settle on full games and the filters remove
   ~11% of plays: each volume projection multiplied by the measured unfiltered/filtered
   per-game ratio for that exact stat — a bias correction, not a fudge.
5. Every projection carries **uncertainty bands**; unmodeled risks are **named in writing**
   (injuries, weather, roster thin spots) rather than hidden in the number.
6. Where the data cannot support a projection, the row is **NULL with a one-line reason** —
   and a projection that disagrees with the market is a hypothesis, not an edge, until
   validated. That is the **H1/H2/H3 standard**: three pre-registered hypotheses were killed
   on honest nulls in the props lab before this work began, and the same bar applies.

**What the stack does NOT use, and why:** no proprietary charts republished — ever. PFF
grades, DVOA tables, Next Gen Stats visuals are read to learn and to sanity-check (Seattle
defensive EPA rank matched The Athletic's TruMedia report; Buffalo EPA rank within filter
noise of PFF's). **Learn, don't lift.** No DVOA formula — proprietary and unverified; compare
qualitatively only (see the JAX/SF case). No whole-highlight video — standing rule from the
2026-09-15 legal check (Richardson v. Townsquare Media, 2d Cir.): real-footage clips stay
2–4 seconds, commentary-led, never the whole play.

**Worked example — Bills vs Lions, 2026-09-17 (market: BUF −5.5, total 54.5; DET down two
starting OL — Mahogany, Miller, ruled out — and both starting safeties — Branch, Joseph,
PUP):** Points — BUF 28 [21,36], DET 25 [17,33] (drive method: own pts/drive × ~10.5 drives);
dropbacks — BUF 35 [28,42], DET 39 [31,47] (script-adjusted); INTs thrown — BUF 0.7, DET 1.0
(DET's 2025 INT luck −2.5 vs expected partially priced as regression); sacks taken — BUF 2.4,
DET 2.6 (DET bumped qualitatively for backup OL — kept out of the number, stated alongside);
score projection BUF 28–DET 25; total ~53 (market 54.5 — agreement); margin: drive method
implies ~BUF −3, EPA method (net EPA/play edge × 63 + 2.0 home field) implies ~BUF −7 —
**they disagree, and that disagreement IS the model uncertainty, not an edge**; market −5.5
sits between them. Kicker/defense props: Bass (BUF) 6.8 [3,10], Bates (DET) 7.2 [4,11] with
long-attempt live-miss notes; BUF team sacks 2.1, DET 2.2; individual player sacks
(Hutchinson, Rousseau) NULL — pressure-to-sack conversion near-pure luck (R² < 0.005), no
false precision. Skill-position props vs consensus: Allen passing yards market 250.5 vs our
201 — UNDER lean, band [135,265] covers the line (market weights Week 1 334 yds + missing DET
safeties, partially unmodeled) — **lean, never a call**; LaPorta receiving yards market 46.5
vs our 79 — OVER lean on role (17.2% when-active share, n=9 active games) — not a strong
call; Gibbs rushing yards market 89.5 vs our 95 — coin flip; 9 other props at the market.
**Language discipline:** lean, never a call; disagreement with the market is a hypothesis, not
an edge. **Verdict (verbatim):** "Nothing here is actionable as a bet... Until then, this is
a scouting document, not a betting one."

**Unmodeled risks kept out of the numbers (named qualitatively):** DET's two backup starting
linemen vs Buffalo's top-5 four-man rush — the single biggest game variable; DET's missing
safeties vs Allen — passing upside not in the numbers; Bass rust (zero 2025 kicks, n=1 Wk1);
new-stadium crowd noise on DET's silent counts/audibles, especially with backup linemen; no
opponent adjustment anywhere in the stack; game script — if DET leads, trailing-script
assumptions (61% dropback) invert.

Supporting files in `props-consensus/`: `consensus_lines.csv` (market captures), player
gamelogs (A. St. Brown, D. Kincaid, D. Montgomery, J. Allen, J. Cook, J. Gibbs, J. Goff,
J. Williams, K. Shakir, S. LaPorta — 2025), `defenders_2025/2026.csv`,
`agents-draft-eight-posts.md`, `compute_player_stats.py`, `kicker-defense-props.md`.

### 7d. Metric theory referenced but not elsewhere detailed

Source: `docs/research/session-handoff-2026-09-12.md` (intelligence-pass coverage) and
`docs/research/competitor-scrape-2026-09-12.md`.
- **Grouping loss** (arXiv 2210.16315): "given the calibration loss, the missing piece to
  characterize individual errors is the grouping loss" — the diagnostic that says whether
  RES=0 is "no signal" or "collapsed signal" (scrape target 12 in wave 2).
- **Calibration ladder:** Platt scaling `p(y=1|f) = 1/(1+exp(Af+B))` (A, B fitted by MLE);
  isotonic objective `sum (y_i - f^i)^2` s.t. `f^i >= f^j whenever f_i >= f_j`; temperature
  scaling `softmax(z/T)` (scikit-learn calibration page, wave-2 target 11).
- **Debiased ECE question:** does the plug-in noise subtraction `max(0, raw - noise)`
  over-subtract when a real gap exists? (intelligence-pass area 1, unresolved).
- **GSE-CPOE / GSE-RYOE / GSE-xYAC:** engine fits its own CPOE/RYOE/xYAC models on nflverse
  play-by-play and proves them against NGS (intelligence-pass area 3; open question whether
  linear regression on play features is adequate vs gradient boosting).
- **GSE Score** (0–100 player ranking): LIVE reads processGrade from nflverse; SAMPLE is a
  pool percentile (open questions: z-score or percentile-of-position? points-per-$1k the
  right value metric?).
- **DFS optimizer:** exact DP over (roster-slot fill state) × (salary bucket), provably
  optimal for the objective; leverage = ceiling/(proj×own) under question; GPP objective
  (ceiling vs top-percentile of simulated outcomes) open; exposure control via greedy
  rejection vs DP-integrated open.
- **The 8-post sweep ranked build targets** (from `2026-09-17/README.md`, AGENTS.md):
  1. FPOE/xFP stack 2. EPA + draft-pick Monte Carlo 3. Hidden yardage 4. Transparent Open
  Havoc 5. Survivor + best-ball EV.

### 7e. Deploy-readiness infra note (Anthropic gate)

Source: `docs/research/anthropic-gate-content-flag-aware-2026-05-21.md`. `scripts/check-deploy-readiness.mjs`
was blocking deploy on an HTTP 401 from the Anthropic ping check; the key was invalid and
browser rotation needed a human step, while every other check was green (DATABASE_URL /
DIRECT_URL Neon, REDIS_URL Upstash, Postgres + Redis reachable, Odds API key valid with
20,000 requests remaining, Stripe TEST key + price IDs, vercel.json crons + security
headers, bootstrap gate sequencing OK). Launch-gate flags at the time:
CANONICAL_HISTORY_ENABLED=true, DERIVED_MODEL_HISTORY_ENABLED=false, PUBLIC_PICKS_ENABLED=false,
FEATURED_PICK_PROMOTION_ENABLED=false, PERFORMANCE_STATS_ENABLED=false, PUBLIC_BLOG_ENABLED=false,
OUTCOME_LEARNING_ENABLED=false — i.e., content surfaces dark. Audit showed no production code
path calls Anthropic when content is dark (`apps/web/lib/content-generator.ts` only fires
when invoked; `apps/web/lib/cockpit/jarvis-data.ts` only string-checks the key; dev-only
diagnostic route). Fix: `checkAnthropic()` reads `process.env.PUBLIC_BLOG_ENABLED` — a
non-200 is `bad` (blocks deploy) only when PUBLIC_BLOG_ENABLED=true; otherwise `warn`
("rotate before enabling content"). Reversal is automatic when the flag flips to true — no
code change, no "remember to put this back" debt. Lesson: deploy-readiness gates must be
**content-flag-aware** — infra checks should not block deployment for subsystems no
production route can reach in the current launch posture.

---

## 8. LESSONS — mistakes caught, standards established, rules that came out of this work

### Mistakes caught (with the correction)

1. **v1.0 CEPT Proposition 1 was ill-posed** (source: `cept/HONEST_CEPT.md` Remark 4): the
   earlier premise assumed each fixed-`i` ratio was "an e-value under H₀" for a single
   unspecified null — not well-posed under performativity. Counterexample recorded:
   interventions a, b with m(1|do(a)) = 0.9, m(1|do(b)) = 0.1, p(1|do(b)) = 0.9; under
   do(a), E[p(Y|do(b))/m(Y|do(b))] ≈ 8.11 > 1. Correction: restated as **Theorem 1** under an
   explicit composite null (R1)–(R2); the correction is kept auditable in the document.
2. **The dropped-set Brier integrity check was mathematically vacuous** (Proposition 6):
   for a dropped pick with p = 1/2 + ε, the realized score is 1/4 ∓ ε + ε²; dropped picks
   satisfy |ε| < δ, so the dropped set's sample Brier lies in
   [1/4 − δ(1−δ), 1/4 + δ(1+δ)] **for every possible outcome sequence** — pinned near 0.25
   deterministically, by the selection rule itself. It cannot work. Replacement: run the
   skill-vs-market e-process and calibration instruments on the dropped set. The blindness
   cuts the direction that matters: dropped picks with p = 0.5, true q = 0.7, market m = 0.4
   beat the market at a compounding e-process log-rate of ≈ 0.10 nats/pick while scoring
   exactly 0.25 — real, discarded edge the check passes.
3. **v1.0 wrote the global base rate π in the selective-publication identity** — the correct
   quantity is **π_δ = E[Y | published]** (Proposition 5 correction). A symmetric filter
   |p − 0.5| ≥ δ can still yield π_δ far from 1/2 when forecasts are asymmetric (worked
   example: P = 0.7 w.p. 0.2, P = 0.45 w.p. 0.8 — global base rate 1/2, but δ = 0.1 publishes
   only the 0.7 picks, so π_δ = 0.7 and BS_pub = 0.21). Validation step 2 now reports π_δ on
   the held-out window.
4. **The deleted "average E-factor 1.031 over ~148 games" was not only unreproducible — it was
   internally inconsistent**: 1.031^148 ≈ 92 < 100 = 1/α; the draft's own numbers never
   cleared the draft's own threshold (adopted from the independent DeepSeek review).
5. **CPOE throwaway bug** (source: `gse-lab/COMPUTATION_NOTES.md`): an early version compared
   completions over ALL attempts to expected over non-throwaways and wrongly made nearly
   every QB negative — caught and fixed; comp_pct, exp_comp_pct, cpoe all computed on the
   cp-available (non-throwaway) subset, with n_cpoe reported.
6. **Pushes were silently flattering the record** (source: `session-handoff-2026-09-12.md`):
   PUSH was structurally unreachable for spreads/totals; published and graded the posted book
   line; calibration bucket win rates were averaging push as half a win (flattering sub-50%
   buckets); correlation WIN_RATE was counting every push as a loss; /api/performance floor
   counts included pushes — all fixed to decided-picks-only, ties resolve against us, published
   bet terms frozen write-once (the card can no longer show −4.5 while we grade −3.0).
7. **Decorative mathematics in the early CEPT draft** (source: `cept/HONEST_CEPT.md` §10):
   non-commutative probability/von Neumann algebras, symplectic geometry/Kostant-Souriau,
   Causal Index Theorem (Atiyah-Singer), Chern class/obstruction theorem, Euclidean
   QFT/holographic duality/Wheeler-DeWitt, "Theorem 4 (Universality)" — all removed with
   reasons; "a shorter true paper is worth more than a longer impressive one."
8. **ever-gauzy recommendation reversal** (source: `2026-09-18-ever-gauzy-reference-architecture.md`):
   "do not build multi-tenancy now" was wrong in the specific direction this project keeps
   correcting — it treated an undecided product decision as a reason to defer foundational
   work whose cost rises with time. Corrected: build the foundation now, gate the product
   decision separately.

### Standards established

- **Every proprietary metric gets a birth certificate** — with source-rights envelope,
  payload-rights classification, metric card, model card, validation report, drift card,
  and a public/private exposure level — before promotion (R&D map § Source rights).
- **The Evidence Readiness Matrix** — factors are ACTIVE / SHADOW_READY / SHADOW_COLLECTING /
  BLOCKED / ABSENT; scoring reads only ACTIVE factors; true EV stays blocked until
  independent fair probability is source-backed and separately promoted (2026-05-21).
- **Shadow-first, then product:** every method becomes a deterministic, tested, documented
  shadow primitive before influencing public claims (R&D map); CEPT's instruments run in
  shadow mode; BAEE updates in shadow only; the learning loop's champion/challenger and
  shadow deployment are the reference (ML brief §15).
- **Pre-registered hypotheses with kill lines:** anything entering the engine carries a
  pre-registered hypothesis with a kill line written on the same line as the prediction, a
  shared test set, fixture-grouped time-ordered folds, a result recorded whether it lives
  or dies (ML brief); the props desk's H1/H2/H3 standard — three pre-registered hypotheses
  killed on honest nulls before the Bills–Lions work (props-consensus).
- **Absent = factor does not fire:** missing data is ABSENT, never zero — factor engine
  convention (intelligence-pass); the `consensus` factor: NEVER fabricate — absent = the
  factor does not fire (scrape-wave-2-results).
- **Never collapse skill/profit/self-honesty into one number** (CEPT §4); never overstate —
  implemented-and-running-in-shadow-mode, validation-pending is the correct statement until
  the validation procedure's step 4.
- **Every number carries league context** — rank, percentile, or average line, or it is cut
  (edge-sheet design brief); every public title, hook, script, sponsor package, and offer
  copy passes commercial-copy and unsupported-performance scans before publication (R&D map).
- **Cite or don't claim:** every legal proposition gets primary-source support; unverifiable
  citations marked UNVERIFIED rather than presented as established (ML brief evidence
  standard; commentary-brand report).
- **Claim-safety and gate law for content surfaces:** content-flag-aware deploy gates
  (Anthropic note); STATS_PUBLIC default OFF with founder-only unlock checklist (StatKing);
  Polymarket hard-hold law (no public Polymarket product, no arb bots, no copy-trade, no
  whale-alert customer features, no guaranteed-edge claims).

### Rules that came out of this work (builder-facing)

1. **Lawful-openings framing:** phrase "loopholes" only as lawful openings, terms-approved
   gaps, open-source analogs, public-data methods, underused rights-cleared sources,
   competitor blind spots, workflow asymmetries, process advantages (R&D map).
2. **Decision doctrine:** confidence is not win probability; GSE Signal Score is decision
   quality, not win probability; no bet is a decision; high EV cannot override missing data,
   stale inputs, unclear rights, drift, or calibration debt (R&D map).
3. **No public claim without settled evidence:** no market-beating performance claims; no CLV
   success claims without sample size and approval (R&D map); any accuracy-theater without
   floors is a brand anti-pattern (prediction-market triage).
4. **No raw restricted payloads as product:** no raw NGS exposure; no raw paid odds resale;
   no raw sports data resale; never re-serve raw restricted feeds as the product; raw NGS
   *row* exposure banned (R&D map). Raw paid odds payloads exposed only where terms allow.
5. **Scraping law:** no restricted scraping, paywall bypass, CAPTCHA bypass, credential
   misuse, fake accounts; check `source-rights-registry.ts` before scraping a fantasy site;
   never put a real book's quotes into a paid SaaS without rights (scrape-wave-2).
6. **Do-not-re-scrape:** wave-2 results are the wiring map — do not re-scrape those URLs
   (scrape-wave-2-results).
7. **Copy law:** no em dashes; no "sports intelligence"/"intelligence" phrasing in public
   copy; no hashtag walls; human voice; team names FULL CAPS when large; BUF/DET only inside
   chart legends and data labels; sharp-friend test for every customer-facing string —
   "would a sharp friend who actually plays DFS say this?" (edge-sheet brief; intelligence-pass;
   memory copy doctrine).
8. **Footage law:** seconds-long transformative clips, telestrated, commentary-led — never
   standalone rips/compilations; 2–4s real-footage clips per the 2026-09-15 legal check;
   no safe "under X seconds" assumption; make every second necessary to active criticism;
   when footage rights are uncertain, rebuild the teaching point as original diagrams or
   Madden captures; quote-press-releases freely, treat footage separately; quote-post,
   never download and re-upload (commentary-brand report).
9. **Learn, don't lift:** PFF grades, DVOA tables, NGS visuals may be read to learn and to
   sanity-check our numbers — never republished, never claimed as computed (our-metric-stack).
   One public PFF grade/stat per post max, labeled "Source: PFF," with link and original
   analysis on top — never paid-only tables or bulk rankings (commentary-brand report).
10. **Projection language discipline:** a projection that disagrees with the market is a
    hypothesis, not an edge, until validated; leans, never calls; disagreement between our
    own methods is model uncertainty, not an edge (game-projections).
11. **No AWS action without approval:** no credentials, no deploy, no account mutation, no
    hosted resources, no DNS, no paid service; AWS artifacts stay local, no-cost,
    credential-free (R&D map).
12. **Fail closed:** restricted, unclear, stale, and raw-payload inputs fail closed
    (source-rights adapters); no-bet governor tests must prove stale inputs, calibration
    debt, drift, and missing data can veto high EV; robust Kelly sizing fails closed (R&D
    map; CEPT).
13. **Repository laws (the nine, session-handoff-2026-09-12):** PRs only, never push main;
    never modify schema.prisma, migrations, .github/workflows, scripts/guardrails, .claude,
    .env*, package-lock.json, .gitignore, .githooks, ai-control-plane; never flip a gate or
    env flag (founder-only); never write a claim you did not observe; never mark DONE
    without DoD commands passing; never `git commit --no-verify`; never install a package,
    run a migration, or touch a database; never fabricate product data; never weaken a guard
    to make a test pass.
14. **Charting honesty (edge-sheet DO NOT LIST):** no pie/donut; no radar/spider; no 3D,
    bevels, gradients, glows, drop shadows; no dual y-axes; no truncated bar axes; no
    rainbow palettes (fourth color must be justified in build notes); no legends where direct
    labeling works; no tick-label soup; no heavy box spines; no orphan numbers; no paragraph
    text; no DejaVu Sans headlines; no fake precision.
15. **Publication-coin discipline (CEPT/ADR-009):** append one entry per epoch BEFORE the
    epoch begins; fill revealedSeed only AFTER the epoch ends; never edit past entries.
16. **Evaluation discipline:** choose δ on an early chronological window, evaluate on a
    later one — a threshold tuned and scored on the same rows is a curve fit (CEPT);
    report π_δ on the held-out window; report effect sizes with sample sizes and proper
    time-ordered splits; report negative results (ML brief).
17. **The ML-regime reminder (ML brief §7a):** evaluate every method against low SNR
    (edges worth having are 1–3 percentage points), an efficient price, small uneven
    samples, non-stationarity, leakage hazards, missing-heavy inputs, and calibration-over-
    accuracy. A method winning large-sample benchmarks and failing here is a negative result.
18. **Priority hygiene:** more repo-visible proof, fewer unsupported claims; every AWS
    artifact remains local and credential-free; every public claim can point to code, docs,
    tests, or settled evidence (R&D map). And the CEPT closing rule: **do not submit to
    arXiv until §6 contains real numbers.**

# 10. Sept 18 Digest

# Sept 18 Digest — Chart Reads, FTN, Full Tables, StatRankings, Props Reverse-Engineering

**Scope:** `~/workspace/vendor/Sports/docs/research/2026-09-18/` (`chart-reads/`, `ftn/`, `full-tables/`, `statrankings/`) plus `2026-09-18-props-reverse-engineering/` (`report.md`, `MISSION-BRIEF-2026-09-18.md`, `notes/`, `firecrawl/`).
**Research date:** 2026-09-18. **Digest compiled:** 2026-09-24.
**Standing directive applied:** exhaustive inclusion — every sports-related item retained with attribution. Overlap with prior digests (`report.md`, `expanded/ngs-digest.md`, `benchmark-digest.md`, `dfs-props-digest.md`, `data-sources-master.md`, `arxiv-sports-index.md`, `learnings.md`) is noted rather than dropped; the target sweep `report.md` carries some of this material already.

---

## 1. Chart-read findings and methods

## 2. FTN data findings

### 2a. FTN Charting API OpenAPI spec (`ftn/openapi.json`)
- Title "FTN Charting", version 1.0.0, **145 paths**, no `servers` array. Auth scheme observed on secured routes: `UserAuthQuery` (query-param user auth). This is a **different, charting-focused spec** from the StatsHub API entries already in `expanded/data-sources-master.md` §24 (SwaggerHub FTN-NFL-API 73 paths on data.ftndata.com; StatsHub 25 POST analytics endpoints). All three surfaces should coexist in the catalog.
- Path families:
  - Core: `/api/key`; `/api/participants/` (participant list, league participants, per-participant, player profile, **player_profile/bulk**, team profile, schedule previous/upcoming); `/api/participant_matching/` (ID resolution); `/api/events/` + `/events/by_charting_status`, `/events/by_condition`, event conditions/charting status, `/event_matching/`; `/api/play_matching/`.
  - Filter-discovery routes (valuable for enumerating charting taxonomies programmatically): `/api/nfl/filters/` × `play_type`, `play_action_type`, `play_action_sub_type`, `play_action_descriptor`, `play_action_result`, `play_action_stat`, `pbp_condition_type` (+`_value`), `pbp_sequence_type`, `charting_play_type`, `offensive_team_scheme`, `defensive_team_scheme`, `charting_position`, `charting_role`, `charting_condition_type` (+`_value`), `charting_action_type` (+`_value`), `charting_action_sub_type` (+`_value`), `charting_action_detail_type` (+`_value`).
  - PBP stats: `/api/nfl/pbp/event/{event_id}`, `/event/{event_id}/participation`, `/api/nfl/pbp/stats/` × event / season base / participation / per-action / per-stat, plus per-participant per-season variants.
  - Charting stats: `/api/nfl/charting/event/{event_id}` (+`/stats`, `/participation`, `/participation/matchups`, `/participation/advanced_stats`), `/api/nfl/charting/stats/season/{season}` × base / participation / **advanced** / per-action / per-detail, plus per-participant variants.
  - Analytics by category: `/api/nfl/analytics/{category}/stats/season/{season}` and `/api/nfl/analytics/{category}/filters/season/{season}`, categories = `passing`, `receiving`, `rushing`, `coverage`, `pass_rush`, `pass_protection`, `rush_defense`, `team_offense`, `team_defense`.
  - Parallel NBA namespace under `/api/nba/` (filters, PBP, charting with shooting/rebounding/screens sub-cuts).
- Observed query params (advanced charting stats route): `season_type`, `week`, `view` (default `player`), `team` (array of ints), season supplied as string in some routes, integer in others — inconsistent typing noted in the spec itself.

### 2b. FTN Data NFL Catalog brochure (`ftn/ftn-data-nfl-catalog.html`)
- ftnfantasy.com/ftn-data-nfl-catalog — "A brochure of every field we chart across Play-By-Play, advanced Charting, and Player Participation." Three feed families: **Play-By-Play, Charting, Participation** ("Explore FTN Data / Contact Sales").
- Play-By-Play feed field taxonomy (partial, captured): `gid` = FTN Game ID, `pid` = FTN Play ID, `detail` = Play-By-Play Description, `off` = Offensive Team, `def` = Defensive Team, `type` = Play Type (RUSH, PASS, KOFF, FGXP, PUNT, NOPL), kickoff fields `knet` (Kickoff Net Yardage), `ktb` (Kickoff Touchback), `kr` (Kick Returner ID), `kry` (Kickoff Return Yardage).
- Charting feed fields: `gid`, `pid`, `detail`, `no_play` (No Play), `off`, `def`, `type` (RUSH, PASS, KOFF, FGXP, PUNT, NOPL).
- Footer metadata: page published 2025-10-02, modified 2025-10-02.

### 2c. Learn-more-about-DVOA (`ftn/learn-more-about-dvoa.html`)
- **DVOA is now available as an add-on in an FTN Data package** ("DVOA NOW INCLUDED … flexible pricing allows all companies to access DVOA").
- Self-description: "sports data company that specializes in delivering extraordinarily detailed and accurate football data with short turnaround times upon game completion"; "robust charting and base collection system"; offerings include traditional statistics plus advanced charted NFL data and player participation delivered via REST JSON API.
- B2B feature list: NFL Premium API; NFL NBA PGA MLB coverage; tools: Prop Shop, same-game parlays, player props, betting models, game projections, Ratcliffe's ranks.

### 2d. Sports-data sales page FAQ (`ftn/stats_sports-data.html`)
- **History depth:** Charting and all-22 participation data back to **2019**; expanded participation back to **2021**.
- **Turnaround:** games charted **~24 hours after completion, with overnight releases** (Sunday games released within ~24h).
- **Full charting API docs:** `charting.ftntools.com/api/docs` (vendor-quoted).
- Marketing claims (attributed, time-varying): **750+ NFL data points**, **20+ years of historical data**, "50% less expensive than competition."
- Scope: every NFL and NBA game, hundreds of data points beyond box score — player participation, route data, defensive coverages, pressure rates; season/weekly/daily/rest-of-season timeframes; custom backend feeds with potential exclusivity.

- Files: `ftn_charting_2022.parquet` (41,643 plays), `ftn_charting_2023.parquet`, `ftn_charting_2024.parquet`, `ftn_charting_2025.parquet` (47,316 plays), plus a `ftn_charting_2025.csv` (47,317 lines = 47,316 + header — one-count header artifact).
