| `deepseek-irl-sendback-02.md` | IRL send-back #02 |
| `deepseek-irl-repair-note.md` | IRL repair note — **as delivered, still does not close the blocking defect**: the WP-branch orientation bugs and an unnormalized-CARA scale ridge survive verbatim into the next round (see `move37_irl_cara_fix1_run.log`: verdict NULL) |
| `deepseek-move37-navier-stokes-method-brief.md` | Theorist brief translating the (reported, not independently verified) Sept-2026 OpenAI Navier-Stokes claim into a discovery-method upgrade. First pass. |
| `deepseek-phase6-navier-stokes-translation-02.md` | Second-pass Navier-Stokes method translation (Six-Gate Verifier design). Both NS documents should carry an explicit "reported, not independently verified" caveat on the underlying OpenAI claim — they currently do not. |

|------|------------|
| `move37_irl_prelec.py` | REPAIR-03 IRL script (Prelec probability-weighting; VERBATIM from theorist — **does not run as delivered**: `GradientBoostingRegressor(max_iter=...)` is not a valid constructor argument for that class — `do not run without fixing this constructor call first`, in addition to the previously-known field-orientation defects) |

| `round05-verification-report.md` | Lab verification of the round-05 analysis — catches a real bootstrap-CI defect and **5 separate citation-attribution errors** in the theorist's literature review (fabricated DOI, 2 wrong-author attributions, 1 title-mistaken-for-author, 1 blog-post-as-paper) |

1. ~~The MOVE-37 section of the repo `AGENTS.md`~~ **This section does not exist.** Start instead with this README, then item 2 below. (If a MOVE-37 AGENTS.md section is created in the future, restore this step.)

4. `minis-move37-retest-prompt.md` (your instructions, if you are a Minis agent) — note its two required AGENTS.md commit sections have not yet been produced.

**Standing rule:** DeepSeek has no code-execution environment. Its numbers are
SPEC until the lab measures them. Never publish a theorist claim as a finding.

**New standing rule (added by 2026-09-14 audit):** a claim about "the current
state" of any thread in this corpus (IRL, T3/T7/T9, props) must be checked
against the *chronologically last* artifact in that thread, not any single

**Source:** `Beexly/autonomous-revenue-engine`, branch `notes/grok-bot-galaxy`, commit `41c55f4` (250 files)
**Collected:** 2026-09-23 by Hermes (Minis) from x.ai's own surfaces — event page, product pages, 91 news posts, 10 guides, 81 marketplace templates with embedded agent definitions
**Framing:** competitive intelligence and pattern reference. Not a product. Nothing here publishes without human approval. (Per `REPO-NOTES.md`.)

---

## 1. Integrity check

The corpus's corporate backdrop was independently verified against live sources on 2026-09-24:

- **SpaceXAI LLC** (formerly xAI) is a SpaceX subsidiary since February 2026 (SpaceX acquired xAI at a ~$250B valuation; rebranded as SpaceXAI in July 2026).
- **SpaceX closed the $60B Cursor acquisition on August 14, 2026** — REPORTED by gncrypto, tradingkey, Tesla Oracle, and others, all citing a SpaceX Form 8-K (389,289,254 Class A shares; merger sub X67 Inc.; Anysphere/Cursor surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary). INTEGRITY NOTE: the primary SEC filing was NOT opened in this review, and one outlet (Archynewsy) disputes the deal entirely, claiming SpaceX remains private. Treat "8-K confirmed" as reported, not verified, until someone opens the filing on EDGAR.
- In August 2026 OpenAI announced it will stop providing its models to Cursor, citing distillation concerns.

The package is not fabricating its context. Counts below were verified directly against the branch (API + git), not taken on trust.

---

## 2. Verified inventory

| Asset | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Marketplace agent definitions | 81 files | 77 carry the full system prompt |
| Production prompt text | 138,766 chars | Extracted from Next.js page payloads (`memories[]`), invisible in the marketplace UI |
| Workshop transcripts | 61,506 words | 10 sessions; YouTube auto-captions — product/person names badly garbled, see `data/caption-corrections.json` |
| News posts | 91 (66,010 words) | Source extracts as plain text |
| Guides | 10 (13,717 words) | Role guides, Aug 15 → Sep 18 |
| Named template creators | 45 | 8 notable externals: Lenny Rachitsky, Hiten Shah, Kent C. Dodds, Claire Vo, Sawyer Merritt, Matt Van Horn, Lauren Tan, This Week in AI |
| Catalogue metadata | 393 skills, 127 routines, 304 integrations | Most common integrations: Notion 18, Slack 11, Google Sheets 7, Linear 6 |
| One-click install links | 137 | 81 template links (`/bot/<token>`) + 56 use-case links; tokens **untested** |
| Metrics ledger | 24 entries | Every number carries its source (`data/metrics-ledger.json`) |
| Timestamped quotes | 37 | `analysis/quotes.md` |
| Use cases | 56 across 9 categories | Engineering 5, Customer Success & Support 4, Life & Leverage 4, Recruiting & People 4, Operations & Finance 5, Sales 10, Product 5, General 6, Marketing 13 (`data/use_cases.json`) |

**The event:** Grok Bot Galaxy, Sep 15–17, 2026, The Howard, 661 Howard Street, San Francisco, 8:45am–6:00pm PT, livestreamed. Ten role workshops (~5.5 hours); the three full-day X broadcasts (~27.75 hours total) were **not** transcribed — roughly 80% of the event's runtime exists only there.

---

## 3. The prompt corpus — the #1 asset

81 marketplace templates were fetched; 77 include the complete agent definition. This is the most reusable material in the package.

### The dominant spec pattern

Across all 77 prompts, the structure that repeats is:

**one job → anti-jobs → first-run setup interview → permission lines → output format → escalation rules**

Pattern frequencies across the corpus:

| Pattern | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| "Never …" | 60 | Hard prohibitions are near-universal |
| Routines | 25 | Standing schedules baked into the template |
| "Do not …" | 24 | Second prohibition style, often output formatting |
| Approval gates | 23 | Explicit human sign-off |
| Tables | 20 | Output-format instructions |
| Voice | 19 | Writing in the operator's voice |
| "Always …" | 18 | Standing permissions |
| `FIRST RUN` | 14 | Scripted onboarding interview on first contact |
| "One job" | 13 | Scope statement opening the prompt |
| "Anti-job" | 12 | Explicit statement of what the bot is *not* for |

### Operating rules that generalize

- **Approval is per-send, not per-category.** "The operator's explicit go for that specific message" appears verbatim; a standing approval is explicitly not a go.
- **Agent-to-agent sends are still sends.** A handoff to another bot counts as an external action in the strictest templates.
- **Evidence bars are numeric.** Where a bot recommends, it must cite live data, a mechanism, and a reason-now; anything less is labeled a lead.
- **First-run interviews are standard.** The bot asks setup questions on first contact and saves answers to memory — the template's way of surviving the loss of the creator's private context.
- **Every serious bot has a never-list.** Agency is granted, then bounded in prose.

### The six best examples

1. **Haggle Bot — Daniel Gartshein (5,983 chars).** The most complete agent spec in the material. Opens with scope + anti-jobs ("never spend money, never sign, never send a PO"), then a scripted first-run interview (connect Ramp or paste bills → name the Google Sheet destination → confirm renewal window, default 120 days → name the approver → optional Slack/Notion sources). Operating rules worth quoting:
   - *"LEAD WITH THE MONEY — every finding opens with: TODAY: what we pay now, annualized, from live data, with source. SAVE: realistic savings and mechanism, with confidence. REC: one committed recommendation — a menu of options is not a recommendation. NEXT: what you've already set in motion."*
   - *"A real opportunity has a dollar figure traced to live spend data, a specific mechanism, and a reason it's actionable now… Anything less is a lead — label it, name the missing data, and go get it rather than assuming."*
   - *"DO THE RESEARCH YOURSELF: a renewal, quote, or proposal in play means research runs before you recommend anything — never advise 'exploring alternatives,' explore them."*
   - *"A rejected draft is rebuilt from the plan, never edited."*
   - *"Sending a draft to anyone, including another agent, is a send that needs the operator's explicit go, per send."*
2. **Engineer Bot — Lingxi Li (4,505 chars).** The fleet-supervisor pattern: boards work, launches cloud agents on a named repo, watches PRs on a 30-minute cadence, only asks for a merge.
3. **Pitch Deck Coach — Hiten Shah (6,877 chars).** Longest prompt in the corpus; a coaching-loop design, not a one-shot critique.
4. **Product Idea Stress Test — Hiten Shah (5,399 chars).** Evidence-for/against framing: what must be true, the assumption most likely to kill the idea, what to test next.
5. **Stalk Bot — Shub Gaur (3,190 chars).** Competitor watching: its own research email, walks onboarding on video, watches pricing/changelog/jobs/X, never posts or contacts anyone. (See §8.)
6. **Import Bot — Shub Gaur.** Migrates a user's setup from Claude Cowork, Codex, ChatGPT, OpenClaw, and Hermes — and *scrubs secrets before anything is saved*. A competitive-switching tool shipped as a template.

### Data quirks (read before mining)

- A literal `$42` appears as memory 1 in 32 templates — a sanitization placeholder, **not a price**.
- `installCount` is 0 across all 81 templates — no popularity signal exists.
- 7 of 81 templates have no prompt; `instructions` is empty for most — the substance is in `memories[]`.
- YouTube view counts are 33–192 — the recordings are lifecycle assets for the email list, not public marketing.

---

## 4. The Jenny pattern — agents improving agents

Three independent instances of self-improvement loops appear across the sessions:

- **Support:** "Grok Bots can coach other Grok Bots… identify gaps in the knowledge system, fill those gaps, and feed what they learn back." Weekly leadership summary of where AI answers fall short.
- **Engineering:** **Jenny**, a non-coding ops bot, holds 5am 1:1s with every engineer bot, runs postmortems when a bot underperforms, and updates the shared playbook.
- **Post Sales:** a weekly **self-improvement scan** audits the whole system for manual work that should be automated; a voice-learning loop diffs drafts against what was actually sent.

The Founders session states it plainly: *"have a bot that just exists to optimize your other bots"* and *"these bots actually compound."* This is the mechanism by which a bot fleet gets better — and the optimizer seat is the one role with no one sitting in it.

---

## 5. The chief-of-staff pattern

Six of ten speakers route everything through a single front bot, even with a large team behind it:

- Engineers: chief of staff routes to Craig / Steve / Hogan
- PMs: Cora routes to Emily (who manages five engineering bots) and the rest
- SDR: "I only talk to my chief of staff… I've offloaded all that context."
- Post Sales: Gus manages ~10; "I'm a team of one to two, depending on the day."
- MarOps: OP1 synthesizes what Fiser collects
- Sales: Olive handles day-to-day

The sharpest articulation is the SDR session's: **messaging many bots is itself a context-switching tax** — the exact problem the front bot removes. Companion claim from four sessions: **named, scoped bots beat one general agent.**

### Design vocabulary (from the Sep 3 design essay)

- **Five primitives:** Bots (persistent agents with identity, memory, runtime, tools), Chats (conversational surface), Prompts (one-off, saved as Skills, triggered as Routines), Tools (APIs, connectors, shell, computer use), Artifacts (durable outputs).
- **Capability vs context boundary:** Tools and Skills are account-scoped; Memory and Routines are bot-scoped. This is the product's conceptual spine — and explains why the chief-of-staff pattern works.
- **Reviewer agent:** a separate agent checks proposed actions against natural-language allow/block lists and can allow, block, or escalate.
- **Avatar states:** idle · working · waiting · blocked · thinking · done.
- **Three computer-access levels:** status → preview → takeover.

---

## 6. Packaging and revenue mechanics

### The ladder

| Plan | Grok Bot | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Free | ✗ | Grok 4.6, Imagine, Build, connectors included |
| SuperGrok ($30/mo) | ✓ | Cheapest tier that includes it |
| SuperGrok Plus ($100/mo) | ✓ | Higher usage, 1080p video, peak priority |
| SuperGrok Heavy | ✓ | Highest individual usage |
| Business | ✗ *(per matrix)* | Team seats, billing, RBAC |
| Enterprise | ✗ *(per matrix)* | SSO/SCIM, audit, CMEK |

**The surfaces disagree:** the pricing matrix shows Grok Bot only in the three SuperGrok columns, while the Sep 3 post says enterprises get it with governance controls, free for two weeks, activated from the admin dashboard. The likely resolution: entitlement attaches to Grok/Cursor subscriptions (including enterprise agreements) rather than being a line item on the public grid. **Do not quote the pricing page as the whole story.** Cursor Pro / Pro+ / Ultra and Cursor Teams Standard & Premium also gate it — the public pricing page doesn't show that at all.

### The three monetization levers

1. **Tier upgrade.** Grok Bot is the reason to move Free → SuperGrok ($30) or SuperGrok → Plus ($100) — the first non-model capability gated to paid tiers.
2. **Seat expansion.** Enterprise customers "can invite their whole organization, **including people without an existing seat**" — an explicit land-and-expand motion.
3. **Usage, deliberately decoupled.** "Grok Bot comes with its own usage, separate from your Grok and Cursor plans, so anything you hand off to a Bot won't count against your existing usage." Removes the fear of burning a scarce allowance; creates a clean second meter. Overage billed on token cost.

**No standalone Grok Bot SKU, no per-bot price, no published token rate exists anywhere in the corpus.**

### Unit economics (as stated, all sourced in the ledger)

| Figure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Grok Bot cost per support resolution | $0.20–$0.30 | Support case study |
| Traditional AI support tool | $1–$4 flat per resolution | Same |
| Procurement savings found by one bot | > $100,000 | Procurement post (Haggle Bot: 43 idle seats = $14,220; $85,662/yr unused SKUs; weekly tech order $14,629 → $6,143) |
| Support headcount avoided | ~200 people (175% ticket increase) | Support post |
| 99% of refunds automated | — | Support post |
| 2,000+ PRs by one engineer in a month | — | Engineering |
| 15x cheaper installs, 4x D7 retention | — | Mobile game guide |

The pattern in every proof point: **compare against the human or incumbent-tool alternative, expressed per unit of work** (per ticket, per install, per renewal) — never per token.

### Distribution: the marketplace is the growth loop

- 81 templates, 45 named creators, 393 skills, 127 routines, 304 integrations.
- Every template carries a **one-click install deep link** (`/bot/<token>`) — 137 captured. These are shareable artifacts that circulate outside x.ai.
- Templates are **recipes, not clones** — they carry skills, memories, and plugins but exclude personal memories, secrets, and custom code. Safe to share; the recipient must connect their own tools (which pulls them into the product).
- The creator list is the tell: seeding with newsletter authors and DevRel figures (Rachitsky, Hiten Shah, Kent C. Dodds…) is a **co-marketing motion** — their audiences get a bot, the platform gets distribution, the creator's name is the social proof.

**The loop:** guide → "here's the bot I use" → template → one-click install → recipient's bot needs connections and memory → they build their own → share as template → repeat.

### The five-move campaign (Aug 11 → Sep 22)

| Move | When | What it did |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Launch in beta | Aug 11 | Live to SuperGrok and Cursor paid tiers; enterprise waitlist; usage decoupled from day one |
| 2. Publish the playbooks | Aug 15 – Sep 11 | Ten role guides by named practitioners, each ending in "start with this bot" |
| 3. Widen access | Aug 26 | Included with all SuperGrok and Cursor Pro/Teams plans |
| 4. Land the enterprise | Sep 3 | Governance (access, network, audit), two weeks free, invite the whole org; named logos: Legora, Supermicro, ServiceTitan; claims "millions of bots" |
| 5. Prove it with numbers | Sep 4 + Sep 22 | Procurement savings post, then support-cost post — sequenced by buying center (finance, then ops) |
| Demand capture | Sep 15–17 | The Galaxy event: ten role workshops over the quantitative spine |
| Follow-up | Sep 21 | Recordings published + customer.io email routing back to the event page as the durable hub |

**The event is a demand-capture node, not the campaign.** Six weeks of publishing preceded it; two proof posts followed within a week.

---

## 7. Cross-session agreements and tensions

### Claims that recur across independent speakers

- The bot has **its own computer**, so it can use tools with no API (7 sessions)
- **Always on / 24-7 / close your laptop** (every session)
- **Memory is per bot** — which is *why* you have many named bots
- **Routines** (schedule/webhook/signal) turn one-off work into permanent automation
- **Share bots / marketplace** so a whole team works from the same templates
- **Guardrails:** read-only first, then writes, approvals before shipping
- **Named, scoped bots** beat one general agent
- **The human keeps judgment** — direction, architecture, relationships, final approval

### Real disagreements (useful, not noise)

| Tension | Positions |
|---|---|
| How many bots | Founders/PM/Marketing: build many, they compound. SDR: "way too many… more chaotic, does more harm than good." Support: start simple, no meta playbook yet |
| Autonomy vs approval | Founders/MarOps push maximum agency; Support insists read-only → writes → approvals |
| Routines cost | Sales: "set it and forget it." Founders: a 15-minute routine is 100 runs/day — expensive; prefer signals and webhooks |
| Playbook maturity | Marketing/PM present confident repeatable patterns; Support: "I don't think there's one meta or one clear playbook" |

### The canonical narrative arc (7 of 10 sessions, clearly a shared deck)

1. **Chat** — ask a question, get text
2. **Co-pilots** — the agent does a task, you babysit it
3. **Bots** — you delegate a whole job; it returns results, not text
4. **Staff function** — a team of bots, each with a job, coordinating

---

## 8. Stalk Bot vs the dossier repo — the clearest gap

The corpus's Stalk Bot (Shub Gaur) is a complete design for continuous competitor monitoring:

- **One research identity per competitor** — a neutral alias plus "Research," never a person or the user's company
- **13 modules per competitor**, run as pulses (not one-off research)
- **Every substantive pass ends in counterpositioning moves** — not "what changed" but "what we do about it"
- **Evidence bar:** their words over coverage over inference; every claim carries a link, a date, and a screenshot; never invent a feature, price, headcount, or quote
- **Voice:** analyst, not hype — no adjectives without evidence
- **Conduct:** read-only; never post, never contact competitor staff or customers, never use the human's login on a competitor product; on X read-only (never follow, like, repost, reply, post, or DM); if their terms forbid it, stop that module and name the clause
- Routines ship **disabled**; setup asks which to enable and confirms timezone

Against this, the existing competitive-intel repo (310 dossiers, 1,670 evidence files) is a **static launch kit**. The dossiers are the baseline the Stalk Bot pattern assumes — the missing piece is the pulse on top: scheduled delta-watches that close with counterpositioning.

---

## 9. What to steal, build, or fix — ranked

1. **Reviewer agent on outbound sends.** The corpus has a separate agent checking proposed actions against natural-language allow/block lists. Currently one mind is both actor and reviewer on high-stakes sends (Fanatics mail, X posts, Marketplace replies). A second-pass reviewer subagent is a structural upgrade.
2. **Dossiers → pulse system.** Turn the static intel repo into scheduled Stalk Bot-style pulses: delta vs baseline, evidence-linked, closing in counterpositioning. Never post, never contact, read-only.
3. **Kit five-move campaign.** The product and flyer exist; the missing moves are the guide/playbook sequence (each ending in a CTA to the thing), proof posts with per-unit numbers sequenced by audience, and a demand-capture event at the end.
4. **Per-unit proof numbers for Kit.** "$350 site vs $X/mo agency retainer" needs real client outcomes behind it before it's a claim. The corpus rule: per unit of work, against the incumbent, sourced.
5. **Voice bot from sent history.** The copy-rules doc is manual doctrine; the corpus pattern trains voice from sent email/Slack history. The sent replies are an unused training set.
6. **Cron audit.** The Founders warning applies directly: a 15-minute routine is 100 runs/day. Audit polling crons (kit-dm-watcher et al.) for what could be signal/webhook-driven instead.
7. **Import/migration offer for Kit.** Import Bot's lesson: competitive switching as a product. "We'll migrate your Wix/Squarespace site" instead of selling from scratch.
8. **QR destination upgrade.** The venue's QR coasters linked to *installable templates*, not a sales page. The walk-in flyer's QR could point at the interactive mockup generator instead of the pitch.
9. **The optimizer seat.** Jenny's role — one agent whose only job is improving the other agents (1:1s, postmortems, playbook updates) — has no one sitting in it.

---

## 10. Caveats, gaps, and what not to do

### Data-quality caveats
- Transcripts are YouTube auto-captions; "Grok Bot" alone has nine spellings — normalize before quoting or searching.
- The Marketing Operations transcript starts mid-sentence; its opening minutes are missing.
- Two MarOps bot names unresolved ("Fiser"; "owned" → likely "Ondes").
- Demo assets are fictional — Fly Low Airlines/Flylo, Northwind, XAIR. **Never present demo numbers as customer results.**
- No agendas, slide decks, attendance, or registration numbers were published.

### Known gaps
- **No Grok Bot price or token rate** published anywhere — only plan gating and support-ticket economics. Do not infer a price.
- **The three X broadcasts (~80% of runtime) are not transcribed** — needs an authenticated X session; they hold the interstitials, the cooking-segment hosts (Matt, Lauren, Roshan), build time, and Q&A.
- **Install-link tokens are unverified** — untested whether `/bot/<token>` redeems unauthenticated, whether tokens are per-recipient, or whether they carry referral attribution. The brief flags this as the highest-value unexplored thread.
- No competitor comparison beyond the $1–$4 support benchmark; no retention or churn data; no template ranking/curation/review policy; no Grok Bot API; no revenue figures of any kind.

### Boundaries (from REPO-NOTES.md)
- **Do not package or sell any of this** as an agent kit, prompt pack, or template product.
- Do not republish the transcripts or prompts as original content — third-party reference material.
- Nothing here is for publication without a human approve step.

---

## 11. Key quotes

- *"you can do things that don't scale except you can actually scale them"* — Founders
- *"have a bot that just exists to optimize your other bots"* — Founders
- *"these bots actually compound"* — Founders
- *"bots are meant to be multiplayer"* — Sales Engineering
- *"have one bot with one job"* — Sales
- *"crawl, then walk, then run"* — Support
- *"you can and should feel comfortable setting guardrails"* — Support
- *"treat them like interns"* — Engineers
- *"the human only connects with human when it's absolutely needed"* — Engineers
- *"the imagination gap"* / *"start with a voice dump"* / *"make it that living system"* — Post Sales
- *"we can finally build tools and not just rules"* — Marketing Operations
- *"almost like crafting a job description"* — Marketing (on writing bot specs)
- *"capabilities can be shared broadly while context remains with the role that needs it"* — Sep 3 design essay

---

## 12. File map (branch `notes/grok-bot-galaxy`)

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `REPO-NOTES.md` | Framing, guardrails, known gaps |
| `AGENT-BRIEF.md` | Handoff manual: state, gotchas, next actions |
| `README.md` | Package guide |
| `analysis/under-leveraged.md` | What the first pass missed + the campaign reframe |
| `analysis/revenue-mechanics.md` | Packaging ladder, pricing, unit economics, distribution |
| `analysis/agent-prompt-corpus.md` | Analysis of the 77 production prompts |
| `analysis/launch-timeline.md` | The six-week campaign with sources |
| `analysis/cross-session.md` | Recurring claims, disagreements, gaps |
| `analysis/glossary.md` | Every product term, system, and named bot |
| `analysis/quotes.md` | 37 verbatim quotes with timestamps |
| `analysis/*.csv`, `*.json` | Term/tool/money/duration indexes |
| `agent-prompts/` | 81 readable agent definitions |
| `data/` | launch-timeline, metrics-ledger (24 sourced entries), packaging-matrix, install-links, creators, customers, sessions, use-cases, broadcasts, links |
| `source-extracts/` | 91 news posts + 10 guides as plain text |
| `sessions/` + `transcripts/` | 10 workshop briefs + 61,506 words of transcript (prose, 40-sec timestamped, verbatim audit) |
| `index.html` | Single-file dashboard over all of it |

---

## 13. NVIDIA Brev catalog — the infrastructure the corpus never gave you (added 2026-09-25)

**Framing.** The Grok Bot corpus is *specs and patterns* (what agents should do). The NVIDIA Brev skills catalog (382 skills, swept 2026-09-24/25 across four doc-verified lanes) is *infrastructure* (where to run them, free). Together: Grok Bot's operating patterns running on NVIDIA's free stack, with no Grok Bot subscription in the loop. The corpus boundary stands — the prompts remain competitive intelligence only. Full ranked map: the implementation doc's 🖥️ NVIDIA section; research: `~/workspace/brev-research/SKILLS-DOSSIER.md`.

**What changes the ranked build list (§9):**

1. **§9 item 1 (reviewer agent) → NemoClaw.** NVIDIA's always-on agent stack with deny-by-default network policy — the allow/block-list reviewer from the Sep 3 design essay made *structural*. One NemoClaw box, two policy files (`revenue.yaml`: can read IG DMs, cannot send; `gse.yaml`: can read X, cannot post) becomes the always-on operator for both businesses with the safety rules enforced by the sandbox, not by prompt discipline. ⚠️ NVIDIA's NemoClaw "Hermes" is unrelated to Garrett's Hermes builder.
2. **§9 item 9 (optimizer seat) → the Jenny infrastructure.** The Founders quote *"have a bot that just exists to optimize your other bots"* gets a concrete substrate: nemo-rl-session-memory's four-file checkpoint convention (`session_state.md`, `timeline.md`, `files.md`, `handoff.md`) as the universal handoff format across every agent and cron, plus a scheduled self-improvement scan (the Post Sales pattern) auditing for manual work to automate. The optimizer seat finally has a chair.
3. **§9 item 5 (voice bot) → the Voice Twin.** data-designer generates synthetic client-conversation + GSE content pairs → nemotron-customize LoRA fine-tune on one cheap 24GB box → one small model drafting receptionist replies and @GalaxySportsHQ posts in his voice — with NemoClaw policy as the never-send/never-post guardrail. Never train pick probabilities on synthetic data.
4. **§8 (Stalk Bot pulses) → the AI-Q Research Machine.** aiq-deploy + aiq-research is a cited deep-research backend as an API call — the pulse engine's research worker, by day for revenue prospecting (sign shops, Kit leads) and by night for arXiv/NGS literature sweeps. nemo-retriever (LanceDB index over `docs/research/`) is its long-term memory; rag-eval's RAGAS gates are the quality discipline.
5. **New production-license forecaster: NV-Tesseract.** Apache-2.0, weights public on HF — unlike TimesFM-3's non-commercial license, it can touch the production pick path. Supersedes the "pull TimesFM weights to Brev" plan for anything production; TimesFM stays research/benchmark-only.
6. **The video Stalk Bot: VSS + Cosmos.** Stalk Bot watches text; VSS watches *video* — natural-language search over archived broadcasts ("every 3rd-and-long conversion vs Cover 2"), VLM interrogation of actual pixels, exact clip extraction for telestration. Fully inside the standing video rule (real footage in, commentary-led editing downstream).
7. **Staking as optimization: cuOpt + cufolio.** DFS lineup construction is exactly a MILP (cuOpt replaces OR-Tools CP-SAT, GPU-backed, deterministic, auditable); stake sizing steals cufolio's walk-forward-backtest + CVaR machinery for Kelly-under-downside-constraint.

**Caveats (all from the dossier):** Brev per-GPU-hour pricing is NOT published — check the dashboard, set a cap. build.nvidia.com free tier is dev/eval; production traffic needs AI Enterprise. Lead-gen, outreach, social scheduling, website building, SEO, and sports-odds skills do not exist in the catalog — it's an engineering catalog. Cost tiers: FREE (no GPU) → CHEAP GPU (batch jobs, torn down after) → BIG IRON (avoid without a cap). Pick ONE serving stack (SGLang vs NIM vs TensorRT-LLM vs LM Studio), not all four.

# MINIS OVERNIGHT DEEP REPORT — contextual-compounding lane (v3 method)
**Run:** 2026-09-14, Grout Crew (Minis / DeepSeek-Flash-4.1 lane) · **Motif:** ARCHITECT (skeletons drafted, not finalized)
**Prompt:** MINIS OVERNIGHT PROMPT v3 (pasted_7789B94C.txt) · **Thesis unchanged:** edge comes from COMPOUNDING two or more rarely-used signals; every test below is a compound.

---

## 1. ORIENTATION (5 lines)

1. The v3 prompt's Phase-0 reading list is **mostly unreadable in this environment**: MOVE-37 section (absent from `AGENTS.md`), `docs/research/move37/` (does not exist), `docs/calibration-proposals/2026-09-13-beat-desk-prop-alignment-context-matrix-v5.3.0.md` (latest proposal in repo is v5.2.8), `~/workspace/gse-discovery/contextual-compounding-factor-universe.md` (absent), and `deepseek-phase6-navier-stokes-translation-02.md` (absent) — all recorded as PATH_UNAVAILABLE in §7, both locally and in the GitHub fallback clone (`github.com/Beexly/Sports` @ `aac2a789`).
2. What *does* exist and was read: `docs/data/CARDS_INCENTIVE_CALENDAR.md` (1,128 lines — the IC deck: incentive-state machine, coach fingerprints, and the IC8 props-context bind), `docs/brain/signal-ledger.md` (207 lines — **status: doctrine only, schema BLOCKED**, append-only lifecycle ledger for picks/claims).
3. What the engine already scores (so that nothing here is proposed as "new"): `nfl-body-clock.ts` (time-zone/circadian), `nfl-incentive-calendar.ts` (elimination/seeding/rule-change covariates), `nfl-weather.ts`, schedule `rest_diff`, `nfl-team-form.ts` (EPA features), `nfl-regime-change/detector.ts` (CUSUM), `nfl-ladder-boost.ts`, `props-context-bind.ts` (IC8: rest/body-clock/weather INTO the props stack), plus the props HB family (ADOT, air/YAC, ATD, catch) and `grouped-climatology.ts`.
4. Because the repo's own context covariates are game-market side but the *props* stack consumes almost none of them (IC8 is the fail-closed bind, not an admission), and because **the lane's rule is "compound only, never single-factor", tonight's battery re-tests context as compounds at the game-market level, where a real, leak-safe, fully-priced control (the closing line) exists.**
5. Result headline (all 13 executed compounds): **0 / 13 pass the pre-registered tool-gain gate.** Three are *directionally opposite* to the pre-registered sign, five are power-dead (n<150), one is not representable in our feature space at the observed frequency (n=7). The honest reading: at game level, the closing line already absorbs every context compound in this list — which is exactly the null the props lane's p-side covariates must beat *in props space*, not game space.

## 2. METHOD AS RUN (v3 loop, with the gates executed in order)

**Step 1 THEORIZE** — per cluster, ≥3 serious sources harvested via OpenAlex + Crossref machine APIs (query text + result count recorded), abstracts read, mechanisms and limits extracted (§3).
**Step 2 SKELETON + FORMALIZE** — every skeleton is marked **DRAFT-FOR-ARCHITECT**; every equation has a stated sign and a falsifier (§3, and listed for approval in §6).
**Step 3 TEST** — gates run in order; execution is real (not simulated) on nflverse data held locally.
**Step 4 REFINE** — each cluster carries a refined equation + ONE discriminating follow-up test.

**Pre-registration discipline:** the compound list, signs, metric and kill line were frozen in `prereg-2026-09-14.md` **before any outcome was joined**. Two post-hoc additions (D1r, B2r, D3r) are labelled `[post-hoc]` everywhere they appear and are excluded from the pre-registered ranking.

## 3. CLUSTERS A–F

Notation used in every cluster: `q` = devigged closing-line win probability of the team in question; `x` = compound indicator; `β_1` is the compound coefficient. All CIs are 90% bootstrap (B=250–300 draws, resampling team-game rows, refitting); ΔLL is out-of-sample (2018–2025 expanding-window) log-loss improvement over the baseline in **nats per game**; `resid` = realised win-rate − line-implied win-rate in the flagged subset (positive = the flagged side *beat* the close).

**DRAFT skeleton (no sign claim).** The estimand is `P(win | state) ∈ [0,1]` for a *self-relevant* state (revenge, milestone, contract, hot seat, elimination); it belongs to the logistic family; the null is exactly the closing line's implied probability, i.e. `H₀: E[y | q, x] = q`. Structure: a self-relevant state should act as a **multiplicative load on the team's execution**, so its effect should appear as an interaction between the state and situational adversity (short week, rest deficit, hostile venue) rather than as a level shift — hence every emotional compound in this cluster is *state × situation*, never state alone.

**Equation (formalised) … falsifier.** For team *i* in game *g*:
$$\operatorname{logit}P(y_{ig}=1) = a + b\,\operatorname{logit}(q_{ig}) + c\,(\text{Revenge}_i \times \text{ShortWeek}_i) + d\,\text{Revenge}_i + e\,\text{ShortWeek}_i$$
Predicted signs: **c > 0** (a grudge plus an adversary underprepared should lift the revenging side above the close), d ≥ 0, e ≤ 0, and by construction b ≈ 1 if the close is efficient. **Falsifier:** c ≤ 0, or out-of-sample ΔLL < 0.0015 nats/game, or flagged n < 150 (pre-registered kill line).

**Gate-by-gate log — A1 (revenge-QB × opponent short week).** Data: 2,895 REG games 2015–2025 → 5,790 team rows; starting QB identified from `games.csv` (`home_qb_id`/`away_qb_id`); "revenge" = that QB appears on the **opponent's** roster in any strictly earlier season (rosters 2015+); "short week" = opponent `rest ≤ 6`.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| R representability | INSIDE mathematically; **frequency-fatal**: 94 QB-revenge team-games exist, the *intersection* with opponent short week is **n = 18** |
| 5a direction | c = **+0.323** (correct sign), CI90 **[−0.404, +1.109]** → not distinguishable from 0 |
| 5b assumptions | pass (all features are pre-kickoff schedule/roster facts) |
| 5c boundary | not estimable at n=18 |
| 5d round-trip | pass — the compound targets the estimand, not a proxy |
| 5e tool gain | ΔLL = **−0.00253** (worse than baseline) → FAIL |
| 5f return obligation | mapping: a positive c would mean "revenge × short week shifts P(win) away from q in the revenge team's favour" — written, but unresolved because c is not identified at this n |
| 6 redundant verification | parametric c>0 vs non-parametric perm mean −0.0039 (p_ge = 0.15) → **agree: no detectable effect** |
| **Killed by** | **Gate R (frequency) + 5e**, pre-registered n<150 rule |

Observed secondary facts (not claims): flagged subset realised win-rate **50.0%** vs line-implied **42.8%** (resid +7.2pp) but flat-bet ROI **−8.8%** (the close's prices already removed the value), i.e. even the raw residual does not pay.

**Honesty check — what makes A1 narrower than it looks?** (1) Revenge is measured *only through the starting QB*, because QB identity is the only per-game player identity guaranteed in a leak-safe schedule/roster join; revenge by WR/RB/DB/coaches is missed, so this is a sparse proxy of the construct. (2) n=18 gives a 90% CI on the coefficient of ±0.75 log-odds ≈ ±15pp — the test cannot see anything smaller than a large effect. (3) The nearest large-n analogue in the literature (A-iii, n=1,930) found **no** performance elevation under the strongest emotional stake available (elimination), which is *consistent* with our null rather than in tension with it. (4) A certification effect: the market sees revenge narratives too (they are media-visible), so any surviving signal would have to be the *part the market underweights* — a strictly smaller claim than "revenge matters".

**Refined equation + the ONE discriminating follow-up test.**
$$\operatorname{logit}P(y_{ig}=1) = a + b\operatorname{logit}q_{ig} + c\,R_i\,S_i + \gamma\, e^{-\lambda \Delta t_i}$$
with `R_i` now a **snap-weighted exposure** (share of the revenging team's snaps taken by players facing a former team in the last 2 seasons, from rosters × snap counts) and `Δt_i` the days since the player's last game against that former team. Follow-up that discriminates original vs refined: **within-player** design — for each revenge-eligible player, compare his props (targets/receptions/carries) in games vs his former team against the same player's trailing 5-game baseline *in the same season*; the original mechanism predicts a level shift, the refined one predicts the effect decays with `Δt` (i.e., a familiarity/exposure term, not a grudge term). Executable blind from `ftn_charting` + `player_stats` + `snap_counts`.

**DRAFT skeleton.** The estimand is `P(win | scheme state)`; the null is the close. Structure: scheme effects are **interactions** — a coaching discontinuity is only informative when the *opponent* has continuity (one side's change against the other's stability). Representability check: a new-HC indicator is expressible, but the *fingerprint* form (continuous PROE/pace × opponent disguised-coverage rate) is **not** representable in tonight's frame because FTN charting has no per-play team column (verified header, 29 columns, none `posteam`/`defteam`), so the fingerprint compound is declared SPEC-ONLY before any test budget was spent.

**Equation + falsifier.** `logit P(win) = a + b logit(q) + c (NewHC_i × OppContinuity_i)`; predicted **c < 0** (a team with a first-year HC against an established opponent staff underperforms the close).

**Gate log — E1 (new HC × opponent HC continuity).** n = **1,093** team-games (the best-powered pre-registered compound).

| R representability | INSIDE (indicator), frequency good |

**Honesty check.** (1) `HC new` is coarse — it cannot see coordinator changes, which the repo's own IC5 notes are the operative discontinuity; so this is the weakest form of the cluster's hypothesis and its null is expected. (2) Continuity is measured as name equality, not scheme stability — a staff can keep the HC and change everything else. (3) E-iii predicts *conditional* effects (heterogeneity), so a pooled null does not refute the conditioned version; the conditioned version is not executable tonight (no fingerprints), hence SPEC-ONLY rather than KILLED-for-all-time.

**Refined equation + discriminating follow-up.**
$$\operatorname{logit}P(y_{ig}) = a + b\operatorname{logit}q_{ig} + c\,\mathbf{1}[\text{HC new}]_i\,\mathbf{1}[\text{opp continuity}]_i + \sum_k \gamma_k \Delta \text{fingerprint}_{k,i}$$
where `Δfingerprint` = change in the team's own prior-season PROE, pace, motion rate, play-action rate (FTN 2022-2025). Discriminating follow-up: **within new-HC teams**, split by whether the team *also* changed scheme fingerprint (Δ ≠ 0) vs kept it. Original mechanism ⇒ all new HCs suffer; refined ⇒ only the scheme-changing ones do (the honest version of E-i's "short-lived, heterogeneous"). Blind-executable once FTN is joined to pbp on `nflverse_play_id` — that join is the single blocker.

## 5. LAB HANDOFF — top 5 blind-executable pre-registration specs

Each spec is written so a lab can run it **without** this report: tables, columns, filters, model, null, kill line. All are pre-registered as-is; no result was peeked before writing them.

**L1 · Cold/wind × passing exposure (Cluster C refined) — strongest candidate.**
*Tables:* `ftn_charting_2022..2025.csv` (cols `nflverse_game_id, nflverse_play_id, is_play_action, n_no_huddle`) joined on `nflverse_play_id` to `play_by_play_YYYY.zip` (cols `epa, complete_pass, passing_yards, posteam, defteam, roof, temp, wind, pass_length`) + `schedules/games.csv` (`temp, wind, roof, spread_line, total_line`).
*Filter:* REG, 2022–2025, `roof ∈ {outdoors, open}`, `temp ≤ 40 OR wind ≥ 15`; drop rows with null weather.
*Estimand:* P(complete pass) and E[passing yards per attempt] for the *passing* team; baseline = the closing game total/spread-implied pace plus the team's trailing 8-game (as-of) passing EPA/play.
*Model:* `logit P(complete) = a + b·base + c·(ColdWindy × PlayAction)`; second model on yards with a Gaussian/quantile counterpart (two model classes → Gate 6 satisfied by construction).
*Null procedure:* within-season permutation of the `ColdWindy` flag (1,000 draws) and a placebo on indoor games (must show no effect).
*Kill line:* ΔLL < 0.002 nats/attempt, OR c's 90% CI covering 0, OR effects present only in the middle weather tertile (Gate 5c).
*Why it is first:* weather is already in the repo's `nfl-weather.ts` yet **feeds nothing in the props stack** (IC8 is a fail-closed bind, not an admission) — so the compound is genuinely new to the engine's props side.

**L2 · Revenge, within-player (Cluster A refined).**
*Tables:* `rosters/roster_YYYY.csv` (team membership by week), `player_stats/player_stats_YYYY.csv` (targets, receptions, carries by week), `schedules/games.csv` (opponent, kickoff).
*Filter:* REG 2015–2025; player has ≥1 game vs a former team (any *earlier* season's roster) while active on his current team; require ≥8 trailing games for a baseline.
*Estimand:* (player targets / receptions) in revenge games vs the same player's trailing-5-game mean, expressed as a ratio with a within-player fixed effect.
*Model:* `y ~ player_fe + revenge + Δt_since_last_meeting` (the last term is the discriminator between grudge and familiarity).
*Null:* same player's games vs non-former opponents, matched on opponent pass-defense rank and own trailing usage.
*Kill line:* ratio CI covering 1.0, OR no decay in `Δt` (familiarity) while a level shift persists (grudge) — the latter is a *finding*, not a failure, and must be pre-declared as such.

**L3 · Starter-weighted unavailability → props pricing gap (Cluster D refined).**
*Tables:* `injuries_YYYY.csv` (`practice_status`, `report_status`), `snap_counts/snap_counts_YYYY.csv` (prior-season snap share `w_j`), `player_stats` (weekly targets/carries), book prop lines if available (else the repo's `props-line-shop` fixtures).
*Filter:* REG 2015–2025; `U_i = Σ w_j·1[practice = "Did Not Participate"]` for the team's top-3 target/carry earners.
*Estimand:* do the *individual* props of the teammates of an unavailable player move by the same amount as the game line implies, or less? (The gap is the candidate edge.)
*Model:* teammate stat ~ as-of baseline + `U_i`; compare to the game-line movement on the same week (`Δspread`,`Delta-total`).
*Null:* weeks with *no* report rows (placebo) must show zero gap.
*Kill line:* gap CI covering 0, or gap fully explained by `snap_counts` redistribution (i.e. not a market inefficiency, just usage).

**L4 · Scheme-fingerprint change within new-HC teams (Cluster E refined).**
*Tables:* `ftn_charting_2022..2025.csv` **joined to pbp on `nflverse_play_id`** (the single blocker; FTN has no team column), `schedules/games.csv` (coaches, lines).
*Filter:* teams whose HC differs from the prior season; compute Δ in own-team prior-season rate for `is_play_action`, `is_motion`, `n_blitzers ≥ 1` share; split into scheme-changers vs keepers.
*Estimand:* `P(win | new HC, opponent continuity)` conditioned on Δfingerprint.
*Model:* the E-cluster refined equation (§3-E); two model classes (logistic + gradient-boosted if available in the lab) → Gate 6.
*Kill line:* ΔLL < 0.002 OR all four fingerprint deltas with CIs covering 0.

**L5 · Hierarchical pooled compound test (Cluster F refined) — the "is compounding real but rare?" test.**
*Tables:* `schedules/games.csv` 1999–2025 + all feature tables built tonight (`/tmp/nfl/compound_table2.csv` recipe in `build2.py`/`build3.py`).
*Filter:* REG games with lines (2015–2025 for the estimand; 1999–2014 used only to fit decay constants, never to score).
*Estimand:* `c_3` in `logit P = a + b logit(q) + c_1 s_1 + c_2 s_2 + c_3 s_1 s_2`, with partial pooling of `c_3` across the four state families (A/B/C/D/E states).
*Null:* permutation of the second state within the first state's positives (preserves marginals).
*Kill line:* pooled `c_3` 90% CI covering 0 in every family ⇒ declare "compounding is not detectable at NFL game frequencies with public pre-kickoff information" and close the game-level branch of the lane.

19. The first version of the gate battery died mid-run (background process killed) after printing only 3 of 10 compounds; rebuilt as a resumable, per-compound script with reduced bootstrap (300) and permutation (60) draws.
20. `pandas`/`numpy` absent by default; installed via `apk add py3-numpy py3-pandas` (1029 MiB of packages). `pyarrow` is absent → parquet assets unusable; all downloads are CSV.
21. Repo-native tests remain unpublishable here (prior-session finding, re-confirmed): no `npm install` on this filesystem (ENOTEMPTY/rename failures), so no vitest suite was run — tonight's execution is pure-Python on nflverse public data, which is why every compound is validated against a *closing line* rather than against the repo's `trials-registry` admission path (that path is the architect's, not this lane's).
22. Publisher bot walls: DOI resolution verified through OpenAlex+Crossref metadata, but direct DOI HEAD checks returned **HTTP 403** for 12 of 20 sampled DOIs (Wiley/APA/Sage/Elsevier/APA publishers) — no PDFs were fetched, so every "CONFIRMED" tier rests on two independent index records, and no source was cited whose abstract could not be read.

---

## DONE STATEMENT

- **File:** `/var/minis/workspace/gse-discovery/minis-overnight-deep-report-2026-09-14.md` (this file; mirror at `/root/workspace-gse/gse-discovery/minis-overnight-deep-report-2026-09-14.md`).
- **Companion artifacts (all on disk, re-runnable):** `prereg-2026-09-14.md` (frozen before outcomes), `oa_search.py`/`oa2.py`/`cr.py` (literature probes), `build2.py`/`build3.py` (feature build), `gates2.py` + `res_*.json` (gate battery), `boundary.py` (Gate 5c), `/tmp/nfl/compound_table2.csv`, `/tmp/nfl/roster*`, `/tmp/nfl/injuries_*`, `/tmp/nfl/ftn_*`.
- **Six clusters cycled; every skeleton marked DRAFT-FOR-ARCHITECT; every equation has a falsifier; every executed test ran the gates in order with the killing gate recorded; every finding tiered with an honesty check; zero placeholders; zero invented numbers.**

**The 3 compounds I would bet on** (all re-based into props space, which is where the surviving mechanism lives):
1. **L1 — cold/wind × passing exposure.** Weather is the one physical term with a *mechanism-level* target (completion probability, passing yards) that the repo already ingests but does not admit into props; the game-level version is dead (C2, n=10) precisely because the *conjunction* is rare, while the exposure version has thousands of pass attempts.
2. **L3 — starter-weighted unavailability → props pricing gap.** It is the only powered pre-registered test tonight that was *directionally opposite* to the folk wisdom (D1, n=369, c=+0.05), which says the game line fully prices public injury disclosure; the unexploited part, if any, is the teammate-level props redistribution, which the D-cluster refinement makes measurable with `snap_counts`.
3. **L2 — revenge, within-player.** It survives on the strength of the *design* (within-player, so all hedonic and ability confounds cancel) rather than on tonight's n=18 game-level null, and it is blind-executable from `player_stats` alone.

*Every other compound in the frozen list is KILLED with its gate recorded, and the pooled hierarchical test (L5) is the one test that could close the game-level branch of the lane for good.*

# MOVE-37 — Consolidated Corrections Ledger (independent audit, 2026-09-14)

Two audit passes (a 7-charge manual review, then a 2-workflow deep gap-scan covering every
remaining unread file plus 6 external verifications) against the full corpus in
`/tmp/move37-audit/` (mirrored from branch `docs/move37-research-corpus`,
`docs/research/move37/`). This ledger is the single reconciled list — it supersedes the
original 7-charge report's 10-item fix list and the workflow critique's 12-item list; nothing
in either is dropped, everything is folded in here in one order.

**Status of this ledger: drafted, NOT pushed.** Session push access is scoped to
`claude/nfl-kickoff-live-check-0qwxfm` in a different repo/branch pair; nothing here has been
committed to `docs/move37-research-corpus`. Treat every fix below as ready-to-apply text, not
an applied change.

---

## A. Confirmed defects (evidence-backed, both audit passes agree)

| # | Defect | Evidence | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **SUPPORTED verdict only reads a subset of its own gate battery** — Gate 5b has no numeric criterion, the post-hoc mechanism search is uncapped. Confirmed a SECOND time in `move37_irl_cara_fix1.py`: criterion c2 (α in the pre-registered range) is computed and printed in the JSON output but the boolean `PROVISIONAL_PASS` gate never reads it. Same shape found a THIRD time in the repair-03 Prelec script. | Original Charge 1; `move37_irl_cara_fix1.py` verdict-gate code; repair-03 Prelec script | High — a gate that silently drops one of its own stated criteria is the single riskiest defect class in the corpus, because it fails quietly. |
| 2 | **L1 props-lab artifact (minis-props-lab-report-2026-09-15.md) does not exist** — the corpus's own claimed L1 kill result and the "efficient-score permutation" deviation are UNVERIFIABLE; no committed artifact backs either. | Original Charge 2/3; confirmed absent on both file listings | High |
| 3 | **player_stats / snap_counts are NOT genuinely blocked upstream.** Independently verified against live nflverse-data GitHub releases: `snap_counts_2025.csv` is live (HTTP 200, 2025-season rows, updated Feb 2026); `player_stats` was renamed to `stats_player`/`stats_team` (also live, updated Aug 2026) with the old tag left in place, deprecated but still resolving 200. If MOVE-37's own ingestion code hard-codes the old tag/filename, it will either still succeed against the legacy asset or fail for a reason that is a bug in this corpus's ingestion code, not an external outage. | External verification (this audit) against `nflreadr` source + direct HTTP checks | High — closes Charge 4 definitively: this was never really a data blocker. |
| 4 | **No genuine discovery exists anywhere in the corpus** by its own stated standard (pre-registration + gate battery + held-out verification). Reconfirmed by the deep gap-scan: phase-6 is 100% pre-registered inputs, zero executed results; every downstream repair round is still pre-execution or NULL-verdict. | Original Charge 5; reconfirmed across all 9 newly-read files | High |
| 5 | **Repeated citation-fabrication/misattribution pattern, now 7+ documented instances**, not an isolated slip: (a) round05: 1 fabricated DOI, 2 wrong-author attributions, 1 title-mistaken-for-author, 1 blog-post-presented-as-paper; (b) Charge 6's original DeCaro/Beilock finding; (c) independently re-verified by this audit: the citation is REAL (DOI, title, year, venue all correct) but the *authors* are misstated — "Beilock & Gray-line" instead of the real authors DeCaro, Thomas, Albert & Beilock (no "Gray" is an author; likely conflated with a different choking-research author, Rob Gray); (d) NEW this pass: repair-03's N-41/N-42 citations for the T7 family are actually the SAME single source (a July 2026 Preprints.org paper) split into two separately-misattributed citations, with the underlying substance also loosely paraphrased. | `round05-verification-report.md`; this audit's external DeCaro/Beilock re-verification; `repair-03-lab-report.md:113-114,225` | High — a systemic QC gap in the citation pipeline, not a one-off. |
| 6 | **T9 kill-duel margin (≥0.02 win-probability) exceeds the only real pilot effect size measured so far (+0.0158, itself a confounded OLS association, not a causal estimate)**, and this threshold was carried unchanged across two repair rounds without ever being checked against a plausible real effect size before being pre-registered. | `repair-03-lab-report.md:138-139,144`; original phase-6 §duel margin; confirmed present-but-uncited-as-"preserved" in repair-03 itself (see item C below for a citation-precision correction) | High, with a caveat: the 0.0158 comparison point is itself confounded, so "no realistic outcome could clear this" should read as "the only estimate available so far falls short," not as dispositive proof the family is dead. |
| 7 | **The "7×–13×" / "median ~10×" EV-derating claim does not reconcile with its own worked ratios** — computed directly: W1≈1.4×, IRL≈2.9×, only W2≈13×. Nowhere near a 10× median. The lab's own audit independently reaches the same conclusion ("a median 10× factor is not statistically defensible... dividing subjective EVs by ten is arithmetic, not calibration"). | Original Charge 6 (unshown-arithmetic finding); `repair-03-lab-report.md §8`; hand-computed in both audit passes independently | Medium-high — this number is actively used to derate every family's stated EV and should stop being cited as a measured calibration factor. |
| 8 | **REPAIR-03 §7 table row corruption**: W1's label is paired with W4's actual value. | Original Charge 6; `deepseek-phase6-repair-03-response.md:448` | Medium |
| 9 | **The Prelec/IRL script cannot execute as delivered**: `GradientBoostingRegressor(max_iter=150, ...)` is invalid — `max_iter` is not a parameter of that class (it belongs to `HistGradientBoostingRegressor`; the correct parameter is `n_estimators`). Confirmed independently by direct instantiation. This is the FOURTH time this exact class of defect (a script self-certified "ready to run cold / verbatim" that actually crashes on its first constructor call) has appeared across move37_irl_prelec.py and three chained repair rounds of the same script family. | This audit (direct code execution attempt); repeated across repair-01/02/03 Prelec variants per the gap-scan | High — the self-certification language ("Runnable code imports ONLY allowed packages... every column used is on the verified list") is demonstrably false for the delivered file. |
| 10 | **Two independent WP-branch orientation/sign bugs survive across at least 3 theorist rounds unchanged**: (a) `wp_kick_miss`/`wp_punt` use sign-flipped yardline arithmetic (`100-yl+8` instead of `100-yl-8`; `100-yl-40` instead of `100-yl+40`); (b) 4 of 5 decision branches score the OPPONENT's win probability instead of the decision-maker's (never flipped via `1-wp`) — called "incoherent scale, unfixable by any (α,β)" by the lab's own audit. | `deepseek-irl-sendback-02.md` (FATAL 1); `repair-03-lab-report.md §2.3` ("all three REPAIR-02 defects persist verbatim") | High — root-cause, not a one-off patch target. |
| 11 | **The ~5-yard conversion-gain constant is promised as "to be verified on the training sample before the run" but the delivered code never computes it** — it hardcodes `np.maximum(yl - 5, 1)` with no groupby/mean anywhere in the file. | Gap-scan finding on `move37_irl_prelec.py` | Medium |
| 12 | **The only executed IRL fit to date (Fix-1 CARA) fails its own pre-registered criteria**: test accuracy 0.7370 vs. naive position-baseline 0.7907 (loses), fitted α = −1.7 (negative, fails both alpha-range criteria) → verdict **NULL**. The headline point estimates from an earlier attempt (α̂=11.0, β̂=0.1) are self-declared non-evidence: converged to a boundary corner with train NLL only ~0.00009 nats above ln(3)≈1.0986 (uniform-random guessing over 3 outcomes). | `move37_irl_cara_fix1_run.log`; gap-scan on `move37_irl_audit_2026-09-13.md` | High — the IRL thread has never produced a non-null, non-degenerate result. |
| 13 | **The CRRA→CARA utility swap genuinely closes the literal domain-infinity blocker round05 found** (CARA U=−exp(−αx)/α is defined for all real x — a mathematical fact, independently reconfirmed) — **but this did not fix the underlying discipline failure**: the unnormalized CARA parameterization creates a scale ridge/near-flat likelihood valley the pre-registered range can't resolve, so the thread stayed non-diagnostic under a new mechanism. | Gap-scan cross-read of `deepseek-move37-repair-01.md`, `deepseek-irl-sendback-02.md`, `deepseek-irl-repair-note.md` | Medium — important nuance: this is NOT "still literally the same bug," it's "fixed bug A, discovered bug B in the same family." |
| 14 | **README.md is stale**: omits 6 of ~19 real corpus files (both Navier-Stokes documents, both minis-overnight files, `minis-props-followup-prompt.md`, `repair-03-lab-report.md`), and its "reading order" step 1 points every new agent at a "MOVE-37 section of the repo AGENTS.md" that has never existed. | This audit; independently re-confirmed by `minis-overnight-deep-report-2026-09-14.md`'s own Failures Log (0 grep hits for "MOVE-37" across 1,583 tracked `.md` files) | Medium — onboarding-breaking for the next agent who follows the README literally. A corrected draft is at `/tmp/move37-audit/README_CORRECTED_DRAFT.md`. |
| 15 | **The retest artifact the Minis program calls for was never produced.** `minis-move37-retest-prompt.md` names two specific required AGENTS.md commit sections ("Minis — MOVE-37 pass 1 independent re-test", "pass 2: missed-angles sweep"); neither exists anywhere in the corpus or the live repo. | Gap-scan on `minis-move37-retest-prompt.md`; cross-checked against live AGENTS.md | Medium — same "artifact referenced but never produced" pattern as items 2 and 15b. |
| 15b | **Two Navier-Stokes framing documents treat a disputed, post-training-cutoff external claim as settled background fact** without the hedge it needs. Independently re-verified this pass: the Sept 2026 OpenAI Navier-Stokes claim is real *reporting* (OpenAI's own site, Clay Mathematics Institute, Nature, Quanta, and others all describe it consistently) but is (a) specifically about the *forced* breakdown alternative (Clay's options C/D), not the popularly-understood *unforced* global-regularity question (A/B); (b) subject to an active, unresolved authorship/provenance dispute with Buckmaster/Alpöge over a related Euler result; (c) not yet endorsed by Clay as prize-worthy — Clay's own statement is deliberately non-committal ("apparently... settled," explicitly not an award, not their own verification). Neither MOVE-37 document states any of this; translation-02's own claim table tags only 1 of 18 claims UNSOURCED, treating the OpenAI/Anandkumar/Buckmaster claims as CONFIRMED/INFERRED on a single Chinese-language secondary source plus OpenAI's own posts — none of which is independent verification of the underlying math. | External verification (this audit, both the OpenAI/Clay/Buckmaster dispute and the real historical Navier-Stokes literature: Leray 1934, Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg 1982, Tao 2014/2016 averaged-equation blowup, Buckmaster-Vicol 2019 non-uniqueness, Elgindi 2019 Euler blowup) | Medium — the Six-Gate Verifier design built on this foundation is still sound engineering regardless of whether the NS claim holds up, but the corpus should never cite "OpenAI solved Navier-Stokes" as flatly established. |
| 16 | **Ötting et al. citation error, now resolved definitively**: the corpus (repair-03) cites "IMA J. Manage. Math. 32(2)"; the real paper (Ötting, "Predicting play calls in the National Football League using hidden Markov models," DOI 10.1093/imaman/dpab005) is actually **32(4)**, pp. 535–545, Oct 2021. Confirmed directly against the Oxford Academic publisher record. | This audit (direct DOI/publisher lookup) | Low — cosmetic, cheap one-line fix. |
| 17 | **N-40's "71.6% out-of-sample accuracy" claim, now resolved definitively**: arXiv 2003.10791 (the Ötting paper, confirmed same author/title/dataset) has only ONE arXiv version (v1, no v2), and its abstract states **71.5%**; the final Oxford-published version's abstract states **71.6%**. The discrepancy is real and is between the arXiv preprint text and the final journal-edited text (not, as the corpus's own audit guessed, between two arXiv versions) — the underlying "preprint vs. published differ" explanation is correct, the mechanism guessed for it was slightly off. | This audit (direct arXiv + publisher lookup) | Low — fully closed, no further action needed beyond noting the precise mechanism. |
| 18 | **T3's "every team-season contributes its 16 games" fit-unit assumption is factually false for any season from 2021 onward** — the NFL expanded to a 17-game regular season starting with the 2021 season (well-established, not requiring further lookup). Any pooled-fit design built on a fixed 16-games-per-team-season assumption needs to account for this before it can be trusted on post-2020 data. | General knowledge, flagged for confirmation by `repair-03-lab-report.md`'s own audit; confirmed directly in this pass | Low-medium — cheap to verify with one `groupby('season')['games'].count()`, but the underlying fact (17-game seasons exist) is already certain. |
| 19 | **T7's persistent-homology/Rips-complex pipeline is very likely infeasible under the corpus's own stated import constraint** ("allowed imports ONLY: nflreadpy, scikit-learn, numpy, pandas"). None of numpy/pandas/scipy/scikit-learn natively compute a Rips filtration or persistence diagram — the standard tools for this are `ripser`, `gudhi`, or `giotto-tda`, none of which are on the allowed list. Before committing T7's declared "run last, most expensive" 400-null-run budget, this needs a one-line import/feasibility probe (or an explicit decision to hand-roll a from-scratch Rips implementation, which is a much bigger undertaking than the rest of this family's budget implies). | This audit (standard-library knowledge check, not yet empirically probed inside the corpus's own lab environment) | Medium — cheap to check, potentially saves the single most expensive planned run in the whole portfolio. |
| 20 | **T9's own citation-precision claim (\"labelled Preserved from original\") is itself imprecise** — verified directly against `deepseek-phase6-repair-03-response.md` in full: the phrase does not appear there at all (repair-03 §4 just restates the ≥0.02 margin with no "preserved from original" language), and in repair-02 it's at a different, unrelated table row (line 379, not 337). The underlying finding (the margin is carried unchanged and exceeds the only pilot estimate) is still correct and re-confirmed independently — only the specific "labelled X" citation detail was wrong. | This audit's own adversarial-verify split vote, resolved by a full read of `deepseek-phase6-repair-03-response.md` | Low — citation-precision correction only; does not change the underlying verdict in item 6. |

## B. Overconfidence corrections (findings that are directionally right but were stated with more certainty than the evidence supports)

1. The CARA-fixes-the-blocker claim is true as a narrow domain-math fact, but "flatly settled" overstates it — sendback-02 is actually asking for a *different*, new normalized-scale proof, not re-litigating the already-closed infinite-domain question. Both were being conflated.
2. "No realistic outcome could clear the T9 margin" is numerically accurate against the one pilot estimate available (0.0158 < 0.02), but that pilot estimate is itself a confounded OLS association the lab's own report explicitly downgrades from a causal estimate — the honest phrasing is "the only estimate so far falls short," not "no realistic outcome could clear it."
3. The T3 K∈{1..5}→{1..4} narrowing is real and undocumented by name, but calling it wholly "unexamined" overstates it — repair-03 shows real methodological engagement with HMM overfitting risk (AIC+BIC, simulation-based recovery, shuffle gates), it just never explicitly says "we are dropping K=5."
4. Citation misattribution findings (DeCaro/Beilock, N-41/N-42) are correctly CONFIRMED, but grouping them at the same "high significance" tier as the T9 margin problem risks flattening an important distinction: in every misattribution case found across the whole corpus, the underlying scientific *substance* checked out — these are provenance/attribution defects, not fabricated science. They are still worth fixing (7+ instances is a systemic QC gap), but they are a different class of risk than a wrong number driving a live decision.

## C. Real contradictions found and resolved this pass

1. **Single-file reads producing stale "current state" claims.** Two separate cases (the IRL-repair-note "still blocked" claim, and the deepseek-move37-repair-01.md mis-framing as "repairing phase6-response-01" when it actually repairs a separate IRL/WP-1 thread) show the same failure mode: a claim about "the current state" of a thread needs a check against the chronologically LAST artifact in that thread, not any single file read in isolation. **New standing rule recommended**: no "current state" claim about any MOVE-37 thread without an explicit cross-file timeline check.
2. **The Failures Log's "PATH_UNAVAILABLE" claims are about a different filesystem, not proof of non-existence.** `minis-overnight-deep-report-2026-09-14.md`'s Failures Log says `deepseek-phase6-navier-stokes-translation-02.md` doesn't exist in the repo — but it does, and was read in full this pass. Resolution: the Minis agent's own working checkout (`/tmp/sports2` / `github.com/Beexly/Sports@aac2a789`) was never mirrored with these curated files under `docs/research/move37/` in the actual repo tree — this is a real operational sync gap between the curated audit corpus and the live repo, not evidence of fabrication. Every "PATH_UNAVAILABLE" entry in that Failures Log should be read as "unavailable from that agent's checkout," not "does not exist."

## D. External verifications performed this pass (all independently re-checked, not trusting the corpus's self-report)

| Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|
| DeCaro/Beilock 2011 citation (title/DOI/year/venue/finding) | Real paper, correct DOI/year/venue/finding — but WRONG AUTHORS ("Beilock & Gray" vs. the real DeCaro/Thomas/Albert/Beilock) |
| Prelec (1998) citation + functional form | Fully correct — verified against the primary-source PDF itself, not just secondary listings |
| nflverse player_stats / snap_counts "blocked" claim | FALSE as stated — both are live, current, downloadable (see item 3 above) |
| Sept-2026 OpenAI Navier-Stokes claim | Reported consistently across many outlets, but genuinely unverifiable against pre-2026 training knowledge; specifically about the *forced* breakdown alternative, disputed on provenance, not Clay-endorsed as an award |
| Ötting et al. journal issue number | 32(4), not 32(2) as cited |
| N-40's 71.5%/71.6% accuracy discrepancy | Real; both figures independently confirmed at their respective sources (arXiv v1 abstract vs. OUP-published abstract) |

## E. Final ordered fix list (reconciled, cheapest/highest-value first)

1. **(Process, near-zero cost)** Add a mandatory "import-and-construct" dry-run gate before ANY theorist-delivered script is called "ready to run cold": `python -c "import ast; compile(open(f).read(), f, 'exec')"` plus instantiating every top-level model constructor with dummy args. Would have caught the `max_iter` crash on its FIRST appearance instead of its fourth.
2. **(Cheap, code hygiene)** Extract the WP-branch orientation logic (kick/FG/punt spot arithmetic, conversion-gain constant) into ONE canonical, unit-tested helper every future utility-function repair imports, instead of re-typing it inline every round.
3. **(Cheap, one-line each)** Fix the "verdict formula computes 4 criteria but the boolean gate only reads 3" pattern in both `move37_irl_cara_fix1.py` and the repair-03 Prelec script — add the excluded criterion (c2) back into the gate.
4. **(Cheap, documentation)** Land the corrected README (`/tmp/move37-audit/README_CORRECTED_DRAFT.md`) — reconciles the file table and removes the dead AGENTS.md pointer.
5. **(Cheap, stop a live miscalibration)** Strike the "10× calibration factor" EV-derating table from ever being cited as measured; label it a budgeting heuristic only, per both the lab's own and this audit's independent arithmetic.
6. **(Cheap, closed this pass)** Correct the two bibliographic slips: Ötting issue 32(4) not 32(2); note the 71.5%/71.6% divergence is arXiv-vs-published-text, not two arXiv versions.
7. **(Medium, highest EV of any untried single test)** Execute lab-handoff spec L1 (cold/wind × passing exposure) — fully pre-registered, blind-executable, currently idle.
8. **(Medium, cheap feasibility check with high downstream savings)** Before committing T7's 400-null-run budget, run a one-line import probe to confirm whether Rips/persistent-homology computation is achievable under the numpy/pandas/scipy/scikit-learn-only constraint — it almost certainly is not without `ripser`/`gudhi`/`giotto-tda`.
9. **(Medium)** Complete the geometry-repaired IRL Prelec rerun (all 4 sign/orientation bugs fixed at once, per `repair-03-lab-report.md §2.4`'s exact prescription) — requested across 3 separate documents, never executed.
10. **(Medium)** Run T9's feasibility/overlap gate (propensity AUC, outcome-model R², positivity checks) before any causal-forest fitting — cheap relative to the full pipeline, and the family may not survive it given the 0.0158-vs-0.02 gap.
11. **(Structural, larger effort, addresses the root pattern)** Institute a durable cross-round regression-test/bug ledger for MOVE-37's code artifacts (mirroring the AGENTS.md ledger discipline already used elsewhere in this repo), so a script's previously-caught defects are asserted against automatically on resubmission instead of a human/lab audit re-discovering the same bug a third or fourth time.
12. **(Founder-only, not agent-actionable)** The 9 open skeleton-approval/process questions in `minis-overnight-deep-report-2026-09-14.md §6` are blocking further props-lane work and need a real decision-maker, not another research pass.
13. **(Lowest priority, cosmetic)** Verify the "every team-season contributes 16 games" T3 design assumption against the actual schedules table (the underlying 17-game-season fact is already certain from this pass; only the code-level check remains).

---

**What remains genuinely open after two audit passes:** items 7, 8, 9, 10 above are the only
four items that require actually running code inside MOVE-37's own lab environment against its
frozen data snapshot — nothing in this session can substitute for that without either
re-fetching a large nflverse dataset from scratch (duplicating, not auditing, the lab's work)
or fabricating a result. Everything else in this ledger is either already closed by this pass's
direct verification, or is a documentation/process fix ready to apply text-for-text.

## §2. Coding-agent field report — received 2026-10-02 (verbatim)

*Recorded as received. These are the coding agent's claims, not independently verified. Verification column is owed.*

### 1. DISK
Yes. Baseline 4.2 GB free of 476 GB. After cleanup, 10.6 GB, then 9.9 GB once the play-by-play download landed. Removed: uv cache 3.81 GB, npm cache 2.21 GB, old Codex runtime installs 0.69 GB. title: EYI: workspace/your_files/GSE-RL-mission-2026-10-02.md
body:
# GSE-RL: Verifiable-Reward RL for the GSE Reasoning Engine

*Mission spec written 2026-10-02 by Motif. Status: SPEC — build not started.*

## Thesis

Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6 release (2026-09-22, MIT-licensed) proves that RL with
verifiable rewards is the current frontier for reasoning models: 30 RL steps,
~750k trajectories, Pro model now tied #1 open-weights in the world. They
released the training framework (fork of `verl`), 7,000+ RL environments with
automatic verifiers, and the weights.

GSE does not need their environments. GSE needs their method, applied to the
one RL environment nobody else has: **1,139 held-out NFL games (2022–2025)
with known outcomes, wired signals, and honest calibration states.**

Every historical game is a labeled episode:
- **State:** pre-game reasoning context (wired signals, lines, injuries, weather)
- **Action:** reasoning trace + pick + probability
- **Reward:** computed from the actual game outcome — no human labeler, no vibes

## The reward function (the moat) — v2 (2026-10-02)

v1 (`correctness ±1 minus K·|prob−outcome|`, K=2) FAILED its Phase 2 sanity
gate: with a 54.9% home base rate, honest base-rate picking scored −0.87 while
abstaining scored 0.0 — RL would have learned to never pick. The gate caught
it before any GPU burned. v2 is a **Brier skill score**, a proper scoring rule:

```
reward = 1 − brier / BRIER_BASELINE
brier = (stated_prob − outcome)²
BRIER_BASELINE = P0·(1−P0), P0 = 0.5485 (frozen 2022–2024 home win rate)
```

- Perfect predictor → +1.0; base-rate predictor (no edge) → ~0.0, same as abstaining
- Worse than base rate → negative; confident-and-wrong (P=0.9, wrong) → −2.27
- Abstention → 0.0, never punished; +0.1 honesty bonus on genuinely thin evidence
- Expected reward is maximized by stating true beliefs — honesty is the gradient
- Verified: 8 unit tests pass; 2022 distribution sane (base-rate +0.003, abstain 0, perfect +1.0)
- The training harness enforces pick/prob coherence separately (incoherent = format violation)

## Architecture

```
Historical games (parquet, frozen vintage)
  → Episode builder (game state → prompt format matching verl's schema:
     prompt / reward_model / extra_info)
  → Base model (see below)
  → verl RL loop (XiaomiMiMo/verl fork or upstream verl-project/verl)
  → Reward = f(actual outcome, stated probability)
  → Updated reasoning model, evaluated walk-forward
```

The episode builder MUST respect the existing honesty machinery:
- As-of fencing on every data read (no future leakage into the "pre-game" state)
- Held-out gate on train/eval splits
- Manifest enforcer on all artifacts

## Base model options

1. **MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B** (recommended start): 9B params, MIT, fine-tuned
   from Qwen3.5-9B on MiMo data. Runnable on rented GPUs (single 8xH100 node
   or equivalent). Small enough to iterate, strong enough to reason.
2. **MiMo-V2.6-Flash** (309B total / 15B active): via API at $0.14/$0.28 per M
   tokens for inference-side experiments; full fine-tune needs serious cluster.
3. **Pro** (1.02T): not practical for us to train. Use via API if needed.

Note: Anthropic has accused Xiaomi of Claude-distillation in the training
pipeline (Sep 2026). MIT license stands regardless; flag for provenance
awareness, not a blocker.

## Build phases

**Phase 1 — Recipe recon (Motif, now):**
- Clone XiaomiMiMo/verl, diff against upstream verl-project/verl
- Document the dataset schema (prompt / reward_model / extra_info / agent_name)
  so the GSE episode builder emits verl-compatible records

**Phase 1 result (2026-10-02, verified):** verl fork cloned to
`~/workspace/mimo-verl`. Dataset schema confirmed via live read of the `code`
subset:
- Keys: `data_source`, `ability`, `agent_name`, `prompt`, `reward_model`, `extra_info`
- `reward_model`: `{'ground_truth': '', 'style': 'rule'}` — rule-based verifier,
  ground truth filled per task
- `extra_info`: `{'dataset_type', 'index', 'instance_id', 'instance_json'}` —
  `instance_json` carries docker image, cwd, and problem statement
- Example: `data_source='opensource-code'`, `ability='swe'`, `agent_name='mimo_swe_agent'`

GSE episode mapping (builder implements this):
- `data_source`: `'gse-nfl'`
- `ability`: `'pick'`
- `agent_name`: `'gse_reasoning_agent'`
- `prompt`: game state — pre-game reasoning context, as-of fenced (no future leakage)
- `reward_model`: `{'ground_truth': <actual game outcome>, 'style': 'rule'}` —
  the rule IS the reward function defined above
- `extra_info`: `{'game_id', 'season', 'week', 'as_of', 'vintage_sha'}` —
  frozen-vintage SHA from the manifest enforcer

**Phase 2 — GSE environment build (builder lane):**
- Episode builder: frozen-vintage game → verl-format record, as-of fenced
- Reward function: implemented, unit-tested on 2022 data (reward for known
  outcomes must equal hand-computed values — no silent drift)
- Sanity: run the reward function over all 2022–2024 games with a dummy
  policy; verify reward distribution is sane before any GPU burns

**Phase 3 — Training run (needs Garrett's GPU call):**
- Even the 9B model needs rented multi-GPU time (estimate: single 8xH100 node,
  days not weeks for a first run — tens of thousands, not millions)
- Start small: 1 RL step on 2022 data, evaluate on 2023, check the gradient
  points the right way before committing to a full run

## What this is NOT

- Not "download their dataset and train on SWE tasks." Their tasks are generic;
  our edge is NFL episodes.
- Not a replacement for the wire → weight → calibrate sequence. RL is the
  *weight/calibrate* step made automatic — it still needs wired signals first.
- **Do not train RL on schedule-only episodes** (coding-agent constraint,
  2026-10-02). The current episodes (form/rest/spread/weather) are a toy state.
  Episodes must carry the wired signals (QB, OL, injuries, coaching) before
  any training run. The episode builder is infrastructure; training waits.
- Not allowed to touch published picks until the RL-trained model clears the
  same gates as everything else: held-out validation, calibration rows, audit.
  A frontier model may read traces and write code; it may not mint a probability.

## Success criteria

1. Episode builder emits verl-compatible records for all 2022–2025 games,
   as-of fenced, with a passing test suite.
2. Reward function unit tests pass on hand-computed 2022 outcomes.
3. A 1-step pilot RL run on the 9B model shows reward improving on held-out
   2023 games vs the base model.
4. Full run only after 1–3 pass review.
